Senses.Explanation: The branch that never sprouts, on which Chan verse sets the real flowering: jade flowers, pure fragrance, the ordination light, the green shade of the one sentence. Baiyu Jingsi, at the master-requested address, raises the whisk: no bias, no host, the temple pole free to be kicked down — leaves and flowers join on the unsprouting branch, phoenix and luan dance in the shadowless grove, no merit involved, great ease obtained; Yingning Zhijing, offering the first incense of his new seat, roots it in the great earth, fragrance from before that shore, blooming on the unsprouting branch, plucked in a flash to offer to founding teacher Sakya; and Pinjixiang Zhixiang, at spring's first stirring, watches all flowers contend in the open sun on the unsprouting branch and strange birds wake from the first eon in the shadowless grove. Yuan'an Liao, asked how to repay his dead mother, answers in one couplet — the gold phoenix dances on the shadowless tree, the jade flower opens on the unsprouting branch; Miyin Zhenchuan, on the day the long rain breaks, verses that on the unsprouting branch the cold wind folds and through the shadowless grove the sagely color fills; Meixi Fudu, conferring the precepts, tethers the wild horse in the shadowless grove and locks the mad monkey on the unsprouting branch; Hansong Zhicao, at a tonsure, sends red flame flying in the shadowless grove and the pure fragrance broadcasting on the unsprouting branch; and Liao'an Qingyu draws the line in the small assembly — with one sentence reaching you, green shade layers on the unsprouting branch; without it, five petals open on the shadowless tree.

Senses.Explanation: Not falling into cause and effect is the mistaken answer that produces the wild-fox fate in Baizhang’s case. The old man says that, in the age of a past Buddha, a student asked whether a person of great cultivation still falls under cause and effect. He answered no, and that denial bound him to five hundred fox lives; he therefore asks Baizhang for a corrective turning word.

Senses.Explanation: Not falling into ranks denies placement on a graded ladder. The phrase enters questions about what remains when holy status, named stages, and even the claim of having no rank are put aside. Qingyuan asks Huineng what work does not fall into ranks and answers that even the holy truths are not undertaken. Jianfu answers with a wax person approaching fire; Ruiyan says there were never ranks to begin with; Furong speaks of a person who receives no imposed order.

Entries.SourceTerm: 不見一法即如來，方得名為觀自在

Senses.PreferredTarget: Not seeing a single thing is the Thus-Come One; only then is one called Avalokitesvara
AlternateTargets: When no one thing is seen, one is the Tathagata and rightly named Guanzizai
SearchAliases: seeing no single thing Tathagata Avalokitesvara
Yongjia verse not seeing one thing Guanzizai
Senses.Note: Yongjia's old verse links seeing no single thing with the names Thus-Come One and Guanzizai. Jieweizhou uses it after describing activity throughout beings and Buddhas; Qianshan explains that non-grasping lets all phenomena appear. Tizong voices it amid images of lamps, pillars, and the temple gate. Baoning asks where Guanzizai is found, while Tianru and Linquan apply it to case discussion. In these contexts, no single thing does not mean an empty absence.

Fushi uses it at the end of a funeral address; Jinian gives it while raising and casting a funeral torch. Yikui turns it into an answer from her whisk, and Songyuan into a memorial response. These are distinct current uses of the inherited line. In another source the line is attributed to the One-Night-Awakened master; the same record sets it beside an apparently contrary warning that failing to see one thing is a grave fault.

Entries.SourceTerm: 不見一法存無見，大似浮雲遮日面

Senses.PreferredTarget: To keep a view of seeing no thing is like a cloud hiding the sun
AlternateTargets: Clinging to nonseeing is like a drifting cloud covering the sun
SearchAliases: clinging to nonseeing cloud hiding sun
Senses.Note: Huineng’s image says that clinging to “seeing nothing” is like a floating cloud masking the sun. Xueguan warns against turning “originally not a thing” into a fixed empty view; Yuanjie applies the verse to someone stuck in a bright but vacant state; Shixi says the warning is for those who still preserve a view, then asks what to do without one; Kongyin distinguishes abandoning knowledge from guarding a blank lack of knowledge. The cloud is the attachment to nonseeing, not the presence of things.

Senses.Explanation: “To keep a view of seeing no thing is like a cloud hiding the sun” warns that even nonseeing can become something held onto. Xueguan applies Huineng’s line to a fixed empty view, while Yuanjie uses it to diagnose a bright but vacant state. Shixi asks what happens without any view to keep; Kongyin warns that discarding knowledge can become another form of clinging.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Not seeing a single color is only half a presentation
SearchAliases: not seeing a single color is only half a presentation
Senses.Note: Yunmen says that seeing no color is only half a presentation and that a full presentation remains. Liangting questions whether a vanished scene counts as the disappearance of color; Jiqi answers with his own gesture. Foyuan warns that the line itself can become a trace, and Shanduo sets it beside another saying. The distinction between half and full keeps the apparent clearing of objects from being mistaken for the whole matter.

Entries.SourceTerm: 不覩雲中鴈，焉知沙塞寒

Senses.PreferredTarget: Without seeing geese among the clouds, how would you know the frontier is cold?
SearchAliases: without seeing geese among the clouds, how would you know the frontier is cold
Senses.Note: The unseen goose and cold frontier image asks how one knows a condition without direct encounter. Tuian uses it to test what seeing a raised fist leaves unresolved; Chuyuan offers it as a sharp reply at an opening ceremony; Huaishen makes it the turn of a sermon on returning to the treasure at home. In the lamp, a questioner gives the same pair to Guangjiao Jingxian and receives a rebuke. These are separate current uses, not repeats of the old Tong’an case.

Senses.Explanation: The fixed sutra negative for all a being fails to register, from moving worlds to its own mind-buddha. Yongming Yanshou, quoting the Tiantai commentary in his Mirror, leaves the dragons and asuras unaware of entering the pore; Dahui Zonggao warns that the dust-laden mind, unaware and unknowing, sins for an instant and drops into the unrelieved depths; the Bloodline Treatise in the Bodhidharma attribution lays the blame squarely: the buddha has no fault, beings inverted and unaware call anything but their own mind the buddha; and Zhuanyu Guanheng remembers that as a frightened child he would, unaware and unknowing, call on Avalokitesvara before anyone taught him. Shishuang Chuyuan's staff swallows the sands-of-Ganges buddhas and lands at one gulp, their beings unaware, while he demands to know where the patch-robed nose is; Zhongfeng Mingben promises that when feelings shed and dust drains away, the striver breaks through unaware and finds the three men already footloose before birth; Pu'an Yinsu quotes the Garland so that every buddha wakes inside one dust-mote's beings while those beings stay unaware; and Wanru Tongwei's whisk tosses this world into another with its beings never noticing, then sets both worlds back where they always stood.

Senses.Explanation: Day follows night before one notices; how could anyone be made young again? Press the urgency of attention as time passes. Guantao Daqi and Yikui Yuankui use the complete saying in distinct recorded teaching turns. Tianshu Xingzhi, Wanfeng Zhishan give further current deployments. The line warns of passing time, not a literal theory of aging.

Occurrences.Kwic: 相逢者少。謂佛鑑曰：既云收得，逮索此珠時，又言無言可對，無理可伸，是如何？忽一日，謂圓悟曰：仰山見東寺因緣，我有語也。東寺當時只索一顆，仰山當下傾一栲栳。圓悟深肯之。法雲杲和尚，遍歷諸家門庭。到圓通璣道者會中，入室次，舉趙州問投子：大死底人却活時如何？投子云：不許夜行，投明須到。意作麼生？杲云：恩大難酬。璣大稱賞之。後數日，舉立僧秉拂，機思遲鈍，滿堂大笑，杲有慚色。次日，堂中特為大眾茶，安茶具在首座寮案上。偶茶瓢子落地，跳數跳，忽悟得答話。機鋒迅捷，無敢當者。復至真淨處，因看祖師偈云：心同虗空界，示等虗空法。證得虗空時，無是無非法。

Senses.Explanation: Night travel is forbidden; you must arrive at daybreak demands arrival while refusing travel in darkness. Yingning Zhijing gives the rule as the words accompanying a slap to a challenger. Yikui Yuankui independently uses it in a direct hall address. Dahui Zonggao's recorded sayings also preserve it as Touzi Datong's answer to a question about a person revived from great death. Zhaojue Daozu gives it as the present conclusion of another verse preserved in a later compilation. Fengxue Yanzhao gives the line as a direct answer to a separate question about all matters being settled.

Entries.SourceTerm: 不許夜行剛把火，直須當道與人看

Senses.PreferredTarget: Do not carry a light secretly by night; show it openly on the road for others to see.
AlternateTargets: Do not carry a light secretly by night, show it openly on the road for others to see.
SearchAliases: do not carry a light secretly by night
Senses.Note: Demand open demonstration rather than private claim or hidden understanding. The light and road are rhetorical images of public testing, not travel instructions.

Senses.Explanation: Do not carry a light secretly by night; show it openly on the road for others to see. Demand open demonstration rather than private claim or hidden understanding. Yushan Shangsi and Doushuai Zongjian use the complete saying in distinct recorded teaching turns. Hanyue Fazang, Yuanjie Jingying, and Xixin Zhaoshui give further current deployments. The light and road are rhetorical images of public testing, not travel instructions.

Senses.Explanation: Do not recognize denies recognition of a person, object, or quality. Weilin Daopei says that living beings do not recognize the true mind and instead take up delusive thinking. Huangbo Xiyun says that Baizhang Huaihai's account lets him see Mazu Daoyi's great function and yet he does not recognize Mazu. Yongming Yanshou preserves a quoted blind-person analogy in which a person born blind does not recognize the color of milk. The sole supplementary lamp records Li Linzong giving a face-to-face answer to Yunfeng Yuanyi. Across these sources, the surrounding object supplies what is not recognized; the compound itself does not name a special state.

Senses.Explanation: "Without recognizing the profound intent, dwelling on stillness is futile" joins a missed point to a wasted effort. Two later masters bring the inherited warning into direct teaching encounters. The anthology prints the line in the poem headed Faith in Mind under Sengcan's name; that heading records an attribution. In J34nB300, a monk quotes this line and Chaozong answers by calling him and challenging his renewed quietist fixation. Zhaozhou answers a monk asking how he teaches with the line. Luyan gives it to a lay reader who says he likes quiet.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB185.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Fushi. In a verse requested by West Hall master Wuqi, Fushi Tongxian pairs self and other with form and shadow. He says that following conditions without changing is hard to distinguish at the point of encounter, while the unchanging following conditions can be met everywhere. He then asks whether, right now, one should say following conditions or unchanging, and gives a new response to that old question. Fushi is the present author; Wuqi is the requester.

Occurrences.ClaimText: 不變隨緣
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB178.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Feiyin. At a birthday hall address requested by layman Governor Wei, Feiyin Tongrong answers questions from a monk before turning to the patron's occasion. He says innate longevity has never gained or lost anything, pairs following conditions with not changing and the unchanging with following conditions, and urges sudden recognition that can transform harmful conduct. He closes with a blessing on long life, strikes the incense table and raises his staff. Feiyin uses the formula to join stable nature with responsive action here.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB203.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yune Xi. At a hall address marking the end of a summer retreat, Yun'e Xi says stillness can hold vast worlds without obstruction. He pairs following conditions without change with an image that cannot be cut open and the unchanging following conditions with ice arising from a drop of water. He then speaks of the retreat's protective practice and says that even the monastery pillars and creatures participate. He closes by challenging whether the assembly has actually reached the monk's point and gives a verse releasing the retreat. Yun'e voices the formula in this present address.

Occurrences.Kwic: ：元來佛法與王法無二。風穴云：見个什麼道理？牧主云：當斷不斷，反招其亂。師云：焦塼打著連底凍。雖然，不是盧陂長老，爭見得風穴老人？不是風穴老人，爭識得牧主个漢？拈拄杖云：者一隊漢，鼻孔眼睛總與穿却了也。是你諸人有事近前，無事珍重。上堂，舉師祖問南泉：摩尼珠人不識，如來藏裡親收得珠即不問，如何是藏？泉云：王老師與汝往來者是藏。祖云：直得不往來時如何？泉云：亦是藏。又問：如何是珠？泉喚師祖，祖應諾，忽然大悟。師云：千鈞之弩不為鼷鼠發機，者僧悟去正是紅爐上一點雪。本覺門下又作麼生？不貪香餌味，可謂碧潭龍。小參。方見立春又是冬至，百歲光陰不消彈指間過了，是你諸人二六時中還曾恁麼猛省也未？盡大地是个解脫門，把手拽不入。周金剛據一條白棒，佛來也打、祖來也打，及乎撞著一个毛頭星到來，接住與他一送，依舊有舌如結、有口如啞。如今冷地思量，者一火魍魎妖精知他是真是假？所以本仁和尚示眾云：老僧尋常不欲向聲前句後鼓弄人家男女。何故？要且聲不是聲、色不是色，高懸羊頭賣狗肉。時有僧問：如何是聲不是聲？也好與一拶。仁云：喚作色得麼？渾鋼打就，生鐵鑄成。僧云：如何是色不是色？矢在弦上，不得不發。仁云

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: ：元來佛法與王法無二。風穴云：見个什麼道理？牧主云：當斷不斷，反招其亂。師云：焦塼打著連底凍。雖然，不是盧陂長老，爭見得風穴老人？不是風穴老人，爭識得牧主个漢？拈拄杖云：者一隊漢，鼻孔眼睛總與穿却了也。是你諸人有事近前，無事珍重。上堂，舉師祖問南泉：摩尼珠人不識，如來藏裡親收得珠即不問，如何是藏？泉云：王老師與汝往來者是藏。祖云：直得不往來時如何？泉云：亦是藏。又問：如何是珠？泉喚師祖，祖應諾，忽然大悟。師云：千鈞之弩不為鼷鼠發機，者僧悟去正是紅爐上一點雪。本覺門下又作麼生？不貪香餌味，可謂碧潭龍。小參。方見立春又是冬至，百歲光陰不消彈指間過了，是你諸人二六時中還曾恁麼猛省也未？盡大地是个解脫門，把手拽不入。周金剛據一條白棒，佛來也打、祖來也打，及乎撞著一个毛頭星到來，接住與他一送，依舊有舌如結、有口如啞。如今冷地思量，者一火魍魎妖精知他是真是假？所以本仁和尚示眾云：老僧尋常不欲向聲前句後鼓弄人家男女。何故？要且聲不是聲、色不是色，高懸羊頭賣狗肉。時有僧問：如何是聲不是聲？也好與一拶。仁云：喚作色得麼？渾鋼打就，生鐵鑄成。僧云：如何是色不是色？矢在弦上，不得不發。仁云

Senses.Explanation: A dragon of the deep pool does not take the fragrant bait. Praise a practitioner who does not bite at attractive inducements. Liao'an Qingyu and Lingrui Fu use the complete saying in distinct recorded teaching turns. Yuan'an Feng give further current deployments. One witness is an active use in a case comment; the saying also occurs passively in older cases. Additional distinct current sources: Shixi Xinyue in X71n1405, Tanfang Shouzhong in X71n1410.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB452.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Lüyan He. Senses.Explanation: Not raising a single thought — is there still fault or not? The probe that prices stillness, sealed with one mountain. At the root, in Yunmen Wenyan's question hall: asked — I do not raise a single thought; is there still fault or not? — one word: Mount Sumeru. Hongzhi Zhengjue, raising it: so marvelous, Yunmen's device — not raising a single thought, answered with Sumeru: the tongue is one strip of flesh, the lips two sheets of skin; it falls into neither knowing, not-knowing, nor right and wrong. Baoning Renyong, in his verse: standing all awry on the ten-thousand-fathom peak, one blink of the eye and you drop off the cliff; whole body without the least harm — in heaven above or among men below, who would dare bury him? Wuyi Yuanlai, in his comment: not raising a thought — a three-foot sword held crosswise; Mount Sumeru — one hair fallen from it; twenty years Boshan could not find his opening, and it was from here he came to know Yunmen. Lanshi Ling, countering: Jingming is not so — if a fellow asked today, I would answer him: the jeweled crown on the heaven-king's head; are this mountain monk and Yunmen the same, or different? settle it, and the staff is handed over with both hands — and he threw it down. Lüyan He, ruling in his address: that monk had no way to turn his body; Yunmen opens a way through everywhere he touches; get it before the case is raised and you walk sideways across the world — failing that, crushed under Mount Sumeru; and the verse: it only wants the person's own right eye open — what has it to do with raising thoughts or not? Shaoyang held up Sumeru the king of mountains — one blow, and empty space splits into seven or eight pieces.

Entries.SourceTerm: 不起纖毫修學心，無相光中常自在

Senses.PreferredTarget: Raise not the slightest mind of cultivation and study; in formless light one is always at ease
AlternateTargets: Without a trace of striving to study and cultivate, one moves freely in light without marks
SearchAliases: no trace cultivation study mind formless light
Senses.Note: The couplet says that, without stirring even a trace of a mind set on cultivation and study, one is at ease in light without marks. Masters use it to close a teaching turn or describe activity free from grasping.

Senses.Explanation: "Raise not the slightest mind of cultivation and study; in formless light one is always at ease" joins release of striving to a state described as light without marks. Masters use the complete line as a conclusion or answer in live teaching. Feiyin closes a hall talk with the couplet; Qiyuan gives it as his answer to a memorial teaching question. Chushi sets it beside eating and resting as needed; Hansong ends an address with it. Lingyin answers a question about the listeners own face with the complete line.

Senses.Explanation: The phrase faults someone for failing to distinguish black from white, and in these records it names failed discrimination in an encounter or in teaching. Xuansha Shibei joins it to 'not knowing auspicious from inauspicious' when rebuking students who only trade replies. Zhu'an Zhenyan applies it to hearers who hide in a formula about forms having no fixed character. A later record quotes Fenyang Shanzhao's stricter pairing, 'right and wrong not distinguished, black and white not divided,' as disqualification from judging for others.

Entries.SourceTerm: 不辭向汝道，恐已後喪我兒孫

Senses.PreferredTarget: I do not refuse to tell you; I fear that afterward I would lose my descendants
AlternateTargets: I would speak to you, but I fear my descendants would be lost thereafter
SearchAliases: I do not refuse to tell you fear losing descendants
Senses.Note: Baizhang asks Guishan to speak without using throat or lips. Guishan asks Baizhang to say it instead. Baizhang replies that he would speak, but fears losing his descendants. The answer makes the danger of a teacher’s explanation part of the question itself. Later masters dispute whether Baizhang and his disciples escaped dependence on words, and some offer their own reply.

Occurrences.Kwic: ：『祗為途路不得力。』復曰：『畢竟如何？』又曰：『楖栗橫肩不顧人，直入千峰萬峰去。』古人恁麼說話，可謂棒打石人頭，嚗嚗論實事。若是那短販行童，漁獵得些子腥羶腐塊，有甚受用？只如道：楖栗橫肩不顧人，直入千峰萬峰去。畢竟是什麼境界？」眾下語不契，師曰：「人情盡處難留跡，家破從教四壁空。」小參。「好看今朝五月六，雨雨風風晴不足，江頭昨競罷龍舟，我愛山間梅子熟。汝既喫了，須還我核來，縱饒道箇百雜碎，我即劈頭與你一棒，曰：種毒了也。」小參。舉：「昔有官人，入鎮州天王院，睹神像，問院主曰：『此何功德？』主曰：『護國天王。』人曰：『祗護此國？遍護餘國？』主曰：『在秦為秦，在楚為楚。』人曰：『前日打破鎮州城，天王向甚處去也？』主無語。若是雲峰，即厲聲喝曰：『者無主孤魂出去。』他若嗔作，但合掌曰：『莫怪相觸忤。』復低聲曰：『幾乎打破鎮州。』」小參。舉：「百丈因溈山、五峰、雲巖侍立次，乃問溈：『併卻咽喉唇吻作麼生道？』溈曰：『卻請和尚道。』丈曰：『不辭向汝道，恐已後喪我兒孫。』又問五峰，峰曰：『和尚也須併卻。』丈曰：『無人處斫額望汝。』又問雲巖，巖曰：『曇晟有箇道處，請和尚舉。』丈再舉，巖曰：『和尚今有也。』丈曰：『喪我兒孫。』者則公案，雲峰秉公直判，主司監守自盜，不免坐罪；溈山不宜把火，五峰不合那贓，雲巖雖有白拈手段，不當公訢朝廷，也不免連名解赴。當時待百丈再舉，但以手掩口，曰：『近日王令甚嚴，不許坐守。』若道得者一語，免致喪我兒孫。」除夕晚參。師以拂子作○相曰：「者是三百六十日最初一句，○，者是三百六十日最後一著，於中還有如是。如是，󱕈如是，󱐞如是，󱐝如是，󳲞如是。設使領略得，則然燈前，然燈後，正然燈，乃至暗機義海無不了然。如不委認，急須明取。◎者箇今晚將你諸人，平日用的，一時舉出，會得的，明年仍有三百六；不會的，豈止為君白了頭。」僧問：「如何是然燈前？」師曰：「你好不伶俐。」：「如何是正然燈？」師曰：「不與你分疏。」曰：「如何是然燈後？」師曰：「寒風嚴入骨。」曰：「謝師答話。」師曰：「雲居羅漢。」小參。舉：「雲巖先和尚，因僧問：『清淨本然，云何忽生山河大地？』先和尚答曰：『我家是廣陵。』奇怪，諸禪德！從來道箭鋒相拄，看孔著楔。老和尚不依本分，合作麼生判斷？理該貶出無生國，任彼分身化作牛。

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 個玉麒麟。向此看得徹，方看得道吾問僧：『甚處來？』曰：『僧堂裏來。』吾曰：『聖僧道甚麼？』僧近前不審。吾曰：『東家作驢，西家作馬。』曰：『過在何處？』吾曰：『萬里崖州。』道吾拈得個猢猻圈圚，東扯西拽，到底勞而無功。者驢漢極欲擺脫韁繩，幾曾出他羅網？呵呵！向此見得透，方見得僧問巴陵：『如何是提婆宗？』陵曰：『銀碗裏盛雪。』巴陵一向水泄不通，偶被者僧一拶，將七珍八寶狼藉殆盡，賺他倚草附木者不少。有能別開一線雲門，兒孫許他猶在。向此轉得身，方知僧問汾陽：『真正修道人，不見世間過，未審不見個甚麼過？』陽曰：『雪埋夜月深三尺，陸地行舟萬里程。』曰：『和尚是何心行？』陽曰：『是你心行。』汾陽者漢，超情離見則不無，抽釘拔楔未夢見在。待問：『真正修道人，不見世間過。未審不見個什麼過？』『高祖殿前樊噲怒，須知萬里絕煙塵。』『和尚是何心行？』『留得五湖明月在，不愁無處下金鉤。』不見百丈云：『併卻咽喉脣吻，速道將來。』溈山曰：『卻請和尚道。』丈曰：『不辭向汝道，恐已後喪我兒孫。』百丈、溈山一般弄巧成拙，不覺家聲喪盡。時有僧問：『併卻咽喉脣吻，請道將來。』但云：『寧可截舌，不向汝道。』又不見德山密云：『但參活句，莫參死句。活句下薦得，永劫無滯。一塵一佛國，一葉一釋迦，是死句；揚眉瞬目，舉指豎拂，是死句；山河大地，更無淆訛，是死句。』問：『如何是活句？』山曰：『波斯仰面看。』大小德山費盡娘生氣力，說到三生六十劫，正是鬼窟活計，直饒道個波斯仰面看，大似赤土塗牛奶。且作麼生是活句？燈籠𨁝跳上青天，露柱魂驚頭腦裂。只如諸公每日聞板聲則赴齋堂，聞報鐘則赴功課，聞普梆則搬柴運米、蒔青刈綠，你道是活句？是死句？是不死不活句？者裏倜儻分明，方許道羅籠不肯住，呼喚不回頭。你看古來尊宿擔荷此事大不容易，三登投子，九上洞山，長慶坐破七個蒲團，趙州二十年不雜用心，不知費盡多少艱難，方得了明心地。即如山僧二九脫白，知有此事，獨住孤峰，力參四載，出山圓具，打七三日，纔得省發。遍叩知識二十餘員，盡皆印可，具大眼目，不過一二。後參百老人於此弁山，被他痛棒，連燈墮地，釋然大徹。隨呈偈云：『探遍諸方最上機，何如直下絕離微？若非一擊連燈落，那得心空及第歸？』輔弼老人一十三載，然後繼席青龍，至今二十年來，七坐名藍，回思從前，如同一日。果

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: ：『祗為途路不得力。』復曰：『畢竟如何？』又曰：『楖栗橫肩不顧人，直入千峰萬峰去。』古人恁麼說話，可謂棒打石人頭，嚗嚗論實事。若是那短販行童，漁獵得些子腥羶腐塊，有甚受用？只如道：楖栗橫肩不顧人，直入千峰萬峰去。畢竟是什麼境界？」眾下語不契，師曰：「人情盡處難留跡，家破從教四壁空。」小參。「好看今朝五月六，雨雨風風晴不足，江頭昨競罷龍舟，我愛山間梅子熟。汝既喫了，須還我核來，縱饒道箇百雜碎，我即劈頭與你一棒，曰：種毒了也。」小參。舉：「昔有官人，入鎮州天王院，睹神像，問院主曰：『此何功德？』主曰：『護國天王。』人曰：『祗護此國？遍護餘國？』主曰：『在秦為秦，在楚為楚。』人曰：『前日打破鎮州城，天王向甚處去也？』主無語。若是雲峰，即厲聲喝曰：『者無主孤魂出去。』他若嗔作，但合掌曰：『莫怪相觸忤。』復低聲曰：『幾乎打破鎮州。』」小參。舉：「百丈因溈山、五峰、雲巖侍立次，乃問溈：『併卻咽喉唇吻作麼生道？』溈曰：『卻請和尚道。』丈曰：『不辭向汝道，恐已後喪我兒孫。』又問五峰，峰曰：『和尚也須併卻。』丈曰：『無人處斫額望汝。』又問雲巖，巖曰：『曇晟有箇道處，請和尚舉。』丈再舉，巖曰：『和尚今有也。』丈曰：『喪我兒孫。』者則公案，雲峰秉公直判，主司監守自盜，不免坐罪；溈山不宜把火，五峰不合那贓，雲巖雖有白拈手段，不當公訢朝廷，也不免連名解赴。當時待百丈再舉，但以手掩口，曰：『近日王令甚嚴，不許坐守。』若道得者一語，免致喪我兒孫。」除夕晚參。師以拂子作○相曰：「者是三百六十日最初一句，○，者是三百六十日最後一著，於中還有如是。如是，󱕈如是，󱐞如是，󱐝如是，󳲞如是。設使領略得，則然燈前，然燈後，正然燈，乃至暗機義海無不了然。如不委認，急須明取。◎者箇今晚將你諸人，平日用的，一時舉出，會得的，明年仍有三百六；不會的，豈止為君白了頭。」僧問：「如何是然燈前？」師曰：「你好不伶俐。」：「如何是正然燈？」師曰：「不與你分疏。」曰：「如何是然燈後？」師曰：「寒風嚴入骨。」曰：「謝師答話。」師曰：「雲居羅漢。」小參。舉：「雲巖先和尚，因僧問：『清淨本然，云何忽生山河大地？』先和尚答曰：『我家是廣陵。』奇怪，諸禪德！從來道箭鋒相拄，看孔著楔。老和尚不依本分，合作麼生判斷？理該貶出無生國，任彼分身化作牛。

Senses.Explanation: Baizhang’s answer joins an offer to speak with a fear for what speaking would do to his disciples. Sanyi and Hansong challenge how Baizhang and Guishan handle a demand to speak without speech. Yuanjie and Pinjixiang return to the three-disciple exchange and ask how the teacher’s answer is to be judged.

Entries.SourceTerm: 不辭向汝道，恐已後無人承當

Senses.PreferredTarget: I do not begrudge telling you, but I fear no one later will be able to bear it.
SearchAliases: I do not begrudge telling you, but I fear no one later will be able to bear it
Senses.Note: The inherited line makes the learner responsible for carrying what is said. The speaker is not withholding a secret formula for its own sake.

Occurrences.Kwic: 超今古類難齊苔封古殿無人侍，月鎖蒼梧鳳不棲。劫外相逢那畔行，靈苗叢裏鐵牛畊東風吹散千巖雪，空畍無雲孤月明。一掬澄潭鏡㨾磨，無風何必自生波？轉身縱不離初際，仔細看來較幾何？跣足披蓑度別岑，相逢切忌話威音，掀翻麟閣動勞泯，擊碎蔆花影象沉。靄靄寒雲籠嶽頂，團團皓月蕩波心，金牛不喫凡閒艸，曉入滄溟無處尋。人靜香消景寂寥，金門不鎖夜迢遙丹墀月滿千峰色，袞袞衣冠萬國朝。霜黃蘆月碧溪秋，水有芙蓉客泛舟春色惱人眠不得，歸來塞雁聽高樓。鶴沖霄漢，鷺出蘆叢，了無位次，迥絕羅籠。月堂照處尊嚴甚，方外誰能造次通？艸遮迥磴絕鳴鑾，雲樹深深碧殿寒，明月自來還自去，更無人倚玉闌干。青原因石頭問：和尚出嶺多少時？師曰：我却知汝早晚離曹溪。曰：希遷不從曹溪來。師曰：我亦知汝去處也。曰：和尚幸是大人，且莫造次。師休去。木人來問青霄路，石女年尊似不聞，𢹂手相將歸故國，暮山岌岌鎖重雲。回首桃源路已非，不禁把袂暮雲迷，泉聲湛湛來霄漢，拂盡煙光萬嶺低。青原問石頭：汝什麼處來？曰：曹溪。師舉拂子曰：曹溪還有者箇麼？曰：非但曹溪，西天亦無。師曰：子莫到西天否？曰：若到即有也。師曰：未在，更道。曰：和尚也須道取一半，莫全靠學人？師曰：不辭向汝道，恐已後無人承當。千輝月云：青原老漢慣打沖霄鸞鳳，善捉海底獰龍，仔細看來，可謂千古作家。石頭雖有格外作略，爭奈被者老漢羅籠帶累，後代兒孫都落在者圈圚裏。即今還有出得底麼？良久，云：逢人不得錯舉。白雲藏玉鳳，紅日照無聊隱隱星攢處，無私鎮九霄。相見錦江頭，相𢹂上酒樓，月闌歌笑罷，回首上扁舟。誰在畵樓西？相逢笑語低，到家春色晚，花落鷓鴣啼。青原問：石頭子何方來？曰：曹溪。師曰：將得什麼來？曰：未到曹溪亦不失。師曰：若恁麼，用去曹溪作麼？曰：若不到曹溪，怎知不失？靈巖儲拈拄杖云：上大人可知禮也，爾小生且道節文在什麼處？卓一下云：自是不歸歸便得，五湖煙景有誰爭？失不失，曹溪路上行人密，雨打風吹動客愁，桃花兩岸牯牛跡。穿小橋，歸人逸，前邨雨過斜陽出，旅亭風動竹枝寒，狼藉青衫仍自溼。青原因僧問：如何是佛法大意？師曰：廬陵米作麼價？博山來云：高低米價，環翠色於奇峰；吞吐廬陵，鍊蟾華於玉樹。須知大用無方，有感斯應。若論青原底佛法，三生六十劫未夢見。翠巖󳭷云：還識青原老漢立地處麼？但見皇風成一片，不知何處有封疆？烏龜三眼赤，祥󲅍一角尖騰雲生暮雨，溪月夜明簾。廬陵米價越尖新，那個商量不挂脣？無限清風生閫外，休將升斗較疎親。

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 超今古類難齊苔封古殿無人侍，月鎖蒼梧鳳不棲。劫外相逢那畔行，靈苗叢裏鐵牛畊東風吹散千巖雪，空畍無雲孤月明。一掬澄潭鏡㨾磨，無風何必自生波？轉身縱不離初際，仔細看來較幾何？跣足披蓑度別岑，相逢切忌話威音，掀翻麟閣動勞泯，擊碎蔆花影象沉。靄靄寒雲籠嶽頂，團團皓月蕩波心，金牛不喫凡閒艸，曉入滄溟無處尋。人靜香消景寂寥，金門不鎖夜迢遙丹墀月滿千峰色，袞袞衣冠萬國朝。霜黃蘆月碧溪秋，水有芙蓉客泛舟春色惱人眠不得，歸來塞雁聽高樓。鶴沖霄漢，鷺出蘆叢，了無位次，迥絕羅籠。月堂照處尊嚴甚，方外誰能造次通？艸遮迥磴絕鳴鑾，雲樹深深碧殿寒，明月自來還自去，更無人倚玉闌干。青原因石頭問：和尚出嶺多少時？師曰：我却知汝早晚離曹溪。曰：希遷不從曹溪來。師曰：我亦知汝去處也。曰：和尚幸是大人，且莫造次。師休去。木人來問青霄路，石女年尊似不聞，𢹂手相將歸故國，暮山岌岌鎖重雲。回首桃源路已非，不禁把袂暮雲迷，泉聲湛湛來霄漢，拂盡煙光萬嶺低。青原問石頭：汝什麼處來？曰：曹溪。師舉拂子曰：曹溪還有者箇麼？曰：非但曹溪，西天亦無。師曰：子莫到西天否？曰：若到即有也。師曰：未在，更道。曰：和尚也須道取一半，莫全靠學人？師曰：不辭向汝道，恐已後無人承當。千輝月云：青原老漢慣打沖霄鸞鳳，善捉海底獰龍，仔細看來，可謂千古作家。石頭雖有格外作略，爭奈被者老漢羅籠帶累，後代兒孫都落在者圈圚裏。即今還有出得底麼？良久，云：逢人不得錯舉。白雲藏玉鳳，紅日照無聊隱隱星攢處，無私鎮九霄。相見錦江頭，相𢹂上酒樓，月闌歌笑罷，回首上扁舟。誰在畵樓西？相逢笑語低，到家春色晚，花落鷓鴣啼。青原問：石頭子何方來？曰：曹溪。師曰：將得什麼來？曰：未到曹溪亦不失。師曰：若恁麼，用去曹溪作麼？曰：若不到曹溪，怎知不失？靈巖儲拈拄杖云：上大人可知禮也，爾小生且道節文在什麼處？卓一下云：自是不歸歸便得，五湖煙景有誰爭？失不失，曹溪路上行人密，雨打風吹動客愁，桃花兩岸牯牛跡。穿小橋，歸人逸，前邨雨過斜陽出，旅亭風動竹枝寒，狼藉青衫仍自溼。青原因僧問：如何是佛法大意？師曰：廬陵米作麼價？博山來云：高低米價，環翠色於奇峰；吞吐廬陵，鍊蟾華於玉樹。須知大用無方，有感斯應。若論青原底佛法，三生六十劫未夢見。翠巖󳭷云：還識青原老漢立地處麼？但見皇風成一片，不知何處有封疆？烏龜三眼赤，祥󲅍一角尖騰雲生暮雨，溪月夜明簾。廬陵米價越尖新，那個商量不挂脣？無限清風生閫外，休將升斗較疎親。

Senses.Explanation: I do not begrudge telling you, but I fear no one later will be able to bear it. The inherited line makes the learner responsible for carrying what is said. Selected current source uses: Feiyin Tongrong in J26nB178, Neishao Zhizhong in J34nB306, Azi Jinwu in J38nB408. The compiled lamp preserves Qianhui Yue's distinct comment on Qingyuan's warning; other lamp copies repeat the old exchange. The complete wording is the entry unit. The speaker is not withholding a secret formula for its own sake.

Senses.Explanation: Baozhi’s line, quoted by Huangbo Xiyun, says that Great Vehicle medicine is taken in vain without meeting a discerning teacher who has appeared in the world. Huangbo recites the line after contrasting accumulated learning with entry through an old master’s teaching gate; he then tells his hearers to learn no-mind in every activity rather than seek another teaching to possess.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB310.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yunsou Zhu. Yunsou Benzhu owns the retained answer: asked the point of the woman's drowning line, he answers in her voice — I only got you, this one son; true, you met no one who knows the sound, but how could I throw you into the water?

Senses.Explanation: Meeting no one who knows the sound: the ferry-woman's drowning line, the emperor's missed exchange, and the halls' maxims on the unhearable — turned by Yunsou into a mother's refusal and priced by Konggu at half a copper coin. Zhenjing Kewen, in the record's raising-the-old-case section: Yantou Quanhuo, after the purge, worked a ferry on the lake; a woman came holding a child and asked — the oar-dance set aside, where did the child in your arms come from? — he struck her, and she said: I bore seven sons, met no one who knew the sound, and this last one too is not needed — and threw him into the water; the master's crack: the despiser of the enemy perishes. Hansong Zhicao, in his raising-and-verse series: Yunmen Wenyan, asked what a buddha is, answered a dried dung pellet — this one pellet has thrown doubt on no few under heaven; a true dragon-devouring garuda has its own sky-splitting swiftness, but the dung-rolling beetle never thinks of leaving the ground — and his verse: the cuckoo sings in the night still and wind clear, each cry within the old misty vines; were there not boundless heartbreak, the regret at meeting no one who knows the sound would not run so deep. Konggu Daocheng, opening the winter binding at the Myriad-Buddha cloister: seize the patriarch's tally and every staff draws blood; hold up the beam of the teaching and every word cuts the trail — scouring out our right-and-wrong there is another stretch of news: meet no one who knows the sound, do not speak it; speak it, and it is not worth half a copper coin — what is it? Half a catty makes eight ounces, two fives make ten. Yongjue Yuanxian, retelling the Guishan story: the monk who had sold his cloth and traveled three thousand li for the laugh heard that Mingzhao Qian had come forth and went straight to bow; asked what Guishan had said, he raised it, and Zhao ruled: Guishan was head straight and tail straight, only he met no one who knew the sound; asked where the words go when the tree falls and the vine dries — that makes Guishan's laugh turn new — and at those words he woke: the laugh had a knife in it; he bowed toward the far mountain and repented. Tianyin Yuanxiu, raising the same ferry case: a woman came with a child in her arms — the oar-dance set aside, where did the child come from? — the master struck, she answered with the drowning line, and his verse: seven sons all thrown to the green waves, the more you puzzle the more it tangles; folk follow their eyes on the clear stream and see only the mother pitying the child, never the old woman. Fushi Tongxian, putting the line to the assembly: the woman bore seven sons, six met no one who knew the sound, and this last one too was not needed, thrown down into the water — having met the one who knows the sound, why is even this one not needed? They could not answer, and he answered himself: the single word knowing is the gate of a hundred calamities. Baichi Xingyuan, at the year-end minor assembly: one firecracker and heaven and earth shake — where will the sprites stick out their heads? He thought on old Wang burning paper, too timid, laughed at Beichan getting dragged into dividing the year — the mountain does not wrong the worthies of old, only the gate-wind differs — is there anyone among you who can deliver? No one answered, and the master ruled: with no guest who knows the sound, talking of the year's cold is labor in vain — and he dragged his staff and broke up the sitting. Yunsou Benzhu, asked the point of the same line, answers in the mother's voice: I only got you, this one son; true, you met no one who knows the sound — but how could I throw you into the water?

Entries.SourceTerm: 不道如來無語，只是無二種語

Senses.PreferredTarget: It is not that the Thus Come One is silent; there are simply not two kinds of speech
SearchAliases: it is not that the thus come one is silent; there are simply not two kinds of speech
Senses.Note: Changqing Huileng says it is not that the Thus Come One has no words, but that there are not two sorts of speech. Baofu asks what such speech is; Changqing replies that a deaf person cannot hear it, and Baofu says this is already a second position before telling him to drink tea. Zukui's verse takes up hearing and tea, Xuedou makes the exchange a case verse, Baiyun asks what Changqing's answer leaves unresolved, and Yanxi says either both speakers are adept or both have missed it. The phrase prevents sacred speech from becoming a separate category while leaving the encounter's challenge alive.

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 不道無禪，只是無師

Senses.Explanation: It is not that there is no Chan; there are no teachers. Huangbo's line tests whether title and crowd really make a teacher. Selected current source uses: Juyun Chuiwan Guangzhen in J29nB239, Juyun Chuiwan Guangzhen in J29nB238, Fushi Tongxian in J26nB185, Jieweizhou Xingzhou in J28nB205. The complete wording is the entry unit. Current masters cite or challenge Huangbo; the line is not their first utterance.

Senses.PreferredTarget: I did not say there is no Chan, only that there are no teachers
SearchAliases: i did not say there is no chan, only that there are no teachers
Senses.Note: A monk asks Huangbo why he says there are no Chan teachers when abbots are teaching everywhere. Huangbo answers that he did not deny Chan, only teachers. Sanyi says the monk’s challenge breaks open the old master’s blockade; Baichi writes a new verse on the case. Sanshan asks whether Huangbo avoids his own verdict, and Yuanjie presses listeners to say where Huangbo’s answer lands.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J40/J40nB488.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dounan Wei. Dounan Wei owns the retained ask-and-verse: right at this moment at home not leaving the road — the on-the-road never-leaving-home line, how does it go? A thousand li to show an old face; meeting, we laugh — whisk cast down, down from the seat.

Senses.Explanation: The never-leaving-home of the Chan records: the founder's road pair — answered with eyes southeast and mind northwest, the white moon scooped from the pool and the Yellow River crossed in dream, worn as the road being home, asked who that one is, and bound into guest and host. Songyuan Chongyue raises the founder's pair — one on the road for whole aeons, never leaving home; one has left home, not on the road — which of the two deserves the offering of gods and men? — and answers: eyes on the southeast, mind on the northwest, Baiyu Jingsi at the Yongfeng hermitage hall adds one more: one always on the road, never leaving home; never leaving home, always on the road — and who is that one? a glance right and left, one shout, descending, Gulin Qingmao fires the pyre verse for his short-stayed attendant — living is putting on the shirt, dying taking off the trousers, the attendant's Chan never given over in words: on the road not leaving home, at home not leaving the road; fire hot and wind stirring, water wet and earth firm — and Huigong Kaixiong answers the ask that quotes the founder's line: asked the one sentence of never-leaving-home — scooping the white moon from the pool; asked the staying-home-yet-on-the-road line — crossing the Yellow River in dream. Meixi Fudu at his leave-taking of the hall: the way-man's walking is like a crane, like a cloud — stopping when he will, going when he will; how far apart are walking and staying? Grasp it and you grasp — never leaving home, always on the road; always on the road, never leaving home — fail, and two straw sandals fierce as a tiger, one bamboo staff alive as a dragon, Yuan'an Liao binds guest and host by it: playing guest, he roams the lakes and seas, yet never leaves home; showing host, he sits cross-legged on heaven and earth — what harm in mixing among the crowd? — then asks the word-free one-line, Chisong Daoling at the carving of his late teacher's record into the canon — one always on the road never leaving home, one never leaving home yet on the road: who is it? — hears the ritual officer answer: far, a hundred thousand; near, not apart from right here — a shout, a blow: one man blessed, the ten thousand matters at peace, and Dounan Wei at the reception: right at this moment, at home not leaving the road — the on-the-road never-leaving-home line, how does it go? A thousand li come specially to show an old face; meeting, we see each other and laugh.

Entries.SourceTerm: 不離當處常湛然，覓則知君不可見

Senses.PreferredTarget: It never leaves this place and stays clear; seek it and you will not see it
AlternateTargets: Always clear right here, it cannot be seen by searching for it
SearchAliases: never leaves this place seek and cannot see
present here but hidden by seeking
Senses.Note: The line says that what is at issue is continuously present where one stands, yet the act of hunting for it as an object prevents seeing it. Masters use the contrast to answer questions about a deceased person’s whereabouts and to turn living students away from a search elsewhere.

Occurrences.Kwic: 座，拈香祝聖罷，乃云：白雲深處，終朝兩眼掛枯松；黃葉落時，旱地一聲轟霹𮦷。禍從天降，回避無門，未免重整襴衫，再呈舊面，向松溪深處開箇小小戲場，竪擲金圈，橫拋栗棘，俾未透者透、未吞者吞。透得過底，銀山鐵壁粉碎無餘；吞得下底，毒藥醍醐融成一味。坐斷千差萬別，頓超十地三賢，處處通方，頭頭得妙，致君堯舜上，再使風俗淳，鳳舞鸞翔，河清海晏。正當恁麼時如何？殊方喜見梯山貢，四野欣聞擊壤歌。復舉保壽開堂，三聖推出一僧，保壽便打公案，師拈云：二大老似鶻拏鳩、如鷹搦兔，收來放去，足有可觀。子細點撿將來，未免俱借這僧鼻孔出氣。若要扶竪臨濟正宗，且緩緩。當晚，小參。一水護田將綠遶，激揚少室家風；萬山排闥送青來，漏泄威音消息。恁麼會得，釋迦不出世，達磨不西來，佛法遍天下，談禪口不開，何必高推臨濟喝似雷奔，獨羨德山棒如雨點？人人脚跟下十日炳煥，箇箇肉髻中百寶光明，無邊剎境靡不流輝，十世古今舉無遺照。日月有顯晦，此則未嘗有顯晦；天地有盈虧，此則未嘗有盈虧。不離當處常湛然，覓則知君不可見。所以道：目前無法，意在目前；不是目前法，非耳目之所到。雖則非耳目之所到，爭柰意在目前？雖則意在目前，爭柰非耳目之所到？這裏一咬咬斷、一󳬇󳬇透，便見夾山眼睛、鼻孔元是自家鼻孔、眼睛。其或未然，莫道西江風浪惡，錢塘更有海門潮。復舉：南泉示眾云：王老師自小牧一頭水牯牛公案。師拈云：馬師道：惟有普願獨超物外。因甚自牧一頭水牯牛？莫擬如何頓放。且道過在什麼處？有人辨得，許你親見南泉。洪首座至，上堂：經誦三千部，曹溪一句忘；塵塵皆寶所，處處是家鄉。雲淨天如洗，潭清月愈光；須知遠煙浪，別有好商量。上堂，召大眾云：直下是，直下是，這邊那邊，滿眼滿耳，綿綿兮長存，湛湛兮不痕，擬議依前隔海門。上堂：雨滴空階，溪流新漲。風起天末，葉墜疎林。喚作物却非物，喚作心不是心。缺齒老胡會不得，九年面壁空沉吟。請後堂并義糓掌會，上堂。摩訶衍法，離四句，絕百非；香飯普熏，遍十方，窮三際。我此一眾總是諸方羅籠不住底，且道為法來耶？為飯來耶？良久，云：莫鈍置。開爐，上堂。竪拂子，召大眾云：這箇如大火聚，近之則燎却面門，是汝諸人如何湊泊？若也湊泊得去，盛夏不熱，嚴冬不寒；其或未然，終日雖在火爐頭，未免總是凍殺底數。上堂，召大眾云：佛法只在日用，日用百發百中。只如諸

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: ○相曰：「圓湛一輪常獨耀，孤光萬古照乾坤。」王有福薦母夏正果，請對靈小參。「生從何來？處處黃花九月開。死從何去？行行鴻鴈飛不住。去去來來合本人，生生死死有根據。只要回頭仔細觀，始知自己安身處。脫體無依任自由，西方東土無疑慮。」為王夫人對靈小參。「閻浮幻體有生死，個裏真常沒往來，一念不生清淨土，萬緣寂靜涅槃臺。休擬議，莫疑猜，差錯毫釐隔九垓，直須恁麼承當去，朵朵蓮花火裏開。莫有承當者麼？為王夫人通一消息。」良久，無人出，驀以拂子打圓相，曰：「了明這點無生意，脫下凡胎入聖胎。」北塔院眾班吉為薦文部大喇嘛請小參。拈拄杖卓一下，曰：「生不離這裏來，死不離這裏去，此處即是他方，他方即是此處。敢問眾等：還識汝師大喇嘛麼？即今在般若拄杖頭邊吹大法螺、繫大法鼓、演大法義、作大佛事，只須剔起眉毛，切忌當面錯過。若是個漢，向般若未動腳前、未開口先直下領略得去，不惟父母師長、佛恩國恩一時盡報了也。既然如是，且道即今大喇嘛在甚麼處？」復卓杖一下，曰：「不離當處常湛然，覓則知君不可見。」吳正省居士請薦先考小參。「思報劬勞意念堅，法輪轉處利無邊，迷雲散盡性天朗，昏障銷融心月圓。迥脫三塗離苦海，頓除八難越人天，金臺逐步相推引，去到西方坐寶蓮。」為印真左善世對靈小參。「本無今有，笑看陽燄翻波；已有還無，喜見空花落影。生也如是，水流原在海；死也如是，月落不離天。」遂以拂子打○相，曰：「且道這個是生耶？死耶？有耶？無耶？」復揮一揮，曰：「若向這裏委悉得去，始識無邊剎海，自他不隔於毫端；十世古今，始終不離於當念。便可以無相中現相、無身處現身。雖居一相中，一相中收他不得；雖居一切處，一切處羅籠他不住。雖然恁麼，猶落在生死窠裏。畢竟如何得不落生死窠裏？」遂振威一喝，曰：「竹密不妨流水過，山高豈礙白雲飛？」古林智禪師語錄卷之二終古林智禪師語錄卷之三侍者正續記錄嗣法門人正巡編輯住遼陽建寧禪寺語錄住遼陽建寧禪寺語錄康熙己巳歲冬十月朔日進院。本寺監院率眾請上堂。「多年不肯順人情，老邁無端顛倒行。自是業緣無避處，且邀明月下襄平。大眾！既到這裏，莫有共相激揚者麼？」良久無出，乃曰：「金剛寶劍，久藏匣中。今朝拈出，孰敢當鋒？妖邪盡喪，狐兔潛蹤。三世諸佛，總立下風。正法眼藏，讓誰立宗？十世古今，一時流通。正恁麼時，天高地厚，海晏河清。

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: ，僧問：「當陽一句埋沒宗風，格外真規超越祖意，請問和尚拄杖子甚麼人得？」師便打，進云：「撐天拄地去也。」師云：「還我端的來。」僧豎拳，師又與一棒，乃云：「英靈衲子、俊俏禪和，葛藤搥斷、踢碎舊窠，不圖成佛作祖，只要跳出網羅，所以羅籠不肯住，呼喚不回頭，古聖不安排，至今無處所，直似橫空寶劍孤光溢目，摩挲鐵柱截斷眾流，用去功不浪施，不用鬼神莫測。畢竟行履在甚麼處？棒頭直下翻身轉，沙界大千一口吞。」小參，云：「踏著當地，不拾人涕唾，不走人舊路，明月簾外不足安身，荊棘林堆一時靠倒，猛虎口裏拔舌，饑鷹爪下奪肉，快刀利劍上明明知有出身之路，轟雷激電處歷歷曉其進退之謀，不惟顯擒龍捉虎之作略，抑且具殺佛滅祖之手段。要是恁麼人，方可入臨濟門下從容話會，故云：垂萬里鉤，駐千里烏騅，布漫天網，打衝浪鯤鯨。不是分外安排，亦非無端造就，蓋道出常情、機通格外，不許瞌睡漢敲磚打瓦，秪要超方眼擊節知音。如是提唱，還會麼？且作麼生說個踏著當地底一句？」卓拄杖云：「不離當處常湛然，覓則知君不可見。」除夜小參，僧問：「百千日月閑中度，三十除宵去復來時如何？」師云：「赤歷地。」僧豎一指云：「其奈者個何？」師打云：「收取去。」乃云：「纖毫脫盡時，理極情忘際，曠劫主人公，突出無眼鼻。所以不見有生，不見有死，不見有涅槃解脫，不見有真如妙性，廓落無依，闃然獨證。且道末後一句意旨如何？明年更有新條在，惱亂春風卒未休。」小參，云：「大道淵源曾無蓋覆，歷歷現成不假思湊。恁麼會得，便見天地同根，萬物一體，古今天地、古今日月、古今山河、古今物理，行也如是、住也如是、坐也如是、臥也如是，乃至折旋俯仰、生死去來，悉皆如是，是法住法位，世間相常住。」驀豎拂云：「劈面來也，急著眼覷。」冬至小參，云：「不涉陰陽底句，還有道得者麼？」僧問：「一陽已度先春信，昨夜寒梅鬥雪開，如何是一陽？」師與一棒云：「急急如律令。」乃云：「群陰剝盡，一陽來復，盡天下人𨁝跳不出。」驀拈拄杖云：「唯有者條拄杖，自古至今，從年竟歲，不可指目。既不可指目，則無陰陽之相，亦無寒暑可述，脫體頓超，千聖頂明，明獨露吞諸物。」乃卓一卓云：「還會麼？」歸方丈。小參，僧問：「空劫已來，和尚在那裏安身立命？」師置拄杖於香几，僧豎拳，師云：「是何消息？」僧禮拜，師云：「暗裏畫符。」乃云：「

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 昌純止火。「晴川歷歷漢陽樹，芳草萋萋鸚鵡洲，風物撩人君莫羨，得休休處且休休。」良久，云：「休，休，一朵曇華插汝頭。」遂攛炬。人塔。「出無礙，入無礙，一顆明珠和月賽，渾身衣裓惹天香，無在之中無不在，且畢竟在何處？咄！若道這裏，便是未免賺殺一船人。」二僧入塔。「恒如自恒如，超塵自超塵，今朝同到此，各各露本真。無縫罅中拶開縫罅，沒藏身處直下藏身，眉稜閃爍光千丈，射透威音那畔人。」為長伊入塔，時直歲先安靈骨。師云：「直歲已為汝入塔了也，教山僧來這裏作甚麼？然雖如是，也要互相證明好。且證明後如何？磕著頭頭契本有，蓮花端的臘中開。」盲僧火。「終日扶墻摸壁行，翻身一踏契無生，雲山海月藏何處？浩浩常光覿面呈。敢問諸人：還委悉麼？」良久，云：「盡道渠儂看不見，誰知有眼更如盲？」為鏡如監寺掩龕。「一片真誠，輔弼叢林年弗倦。半生勤苦，周遊廛市境偏多。慧眼雖曰未圓，要且風光何曾少欠？茲乃末後全提，坐斷千差底時節，是汝諸人還識他落處也無？」卓拄杖，云：「不離當處常湛然，覓則知君不可見。」起龕。「疾如風，明似鏡，拶向前，無坎阱，雖則尋常出入分明，也要山僧與汝打正。」遂引之而出。舉火。「楊岐驢子三隻腳，百億山河都踏著，今朝趁出贈君騎，火鞭頭上光閃爍。」豎起炬，云：「這箇是火鞭，那箇是驢子，鏡監寺還會麼？急須薦取奔騰去，莫待驊騮向後追。」入塔。「知事為疏山造塔，風暖鳥聲碎。山僧為知事入塔，日高華影重。論法固不相侔，窮理且無二致，政當此際，畢竟如何是伊安身所在？」卓拄杖，云：「返照本來塔一座，普天匝地愈崚嶒。」無瑕火。「卞璧無瑕，光連四座，山僧未敢輕許，到此也須試過。且作麼生試？」拋炬，云：「全憑一把乾柴火。」一山入塔。「春日融和，春光明媚，撒手歸來，住安樂地。安樂地既住也，則無解脫可欣，亦無生死可悸，妙用全機不覆藏，一山卓落乾坤翠。」雲虛入塔。「生如浮雲過太虛，死似一漚歸巨海，生死雖然無了期，靈明歷劫不遷改。不遷改，且從這裏覓安身，也勝人間別光彩。」無波火。「波也無，討什麼水？水也無，討什麼波？無波無水風濤起，陸地行舟曾奈何？」呈炬，云：「看看：水中火發也，要會大洋海裏剔金燈，且待山僧先下手。」鐵航藏主火。「東山一句缽羅娘，今日為君重舉揚，掇轉好風航到岸，頭頭無礙是家鄉。雖然。」擊火炬，云：「切不得忘卻這裏。

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 座，拈香祝聖罷，乃云：白雲深處，終朝兩眼掛枯松；黃葉落時，旱地一聲轟霹𮦷。禍從天降，回避無門，未免重整襴衫，再呈舊面，向松溪深處開箇小小戲場，竪擲金圈，橫拋栗棘，俾未透者透、未吞者吞。透得過底，銀山鐵壁粉碎無餘；吞得下底，毒藥醍醐融成一味。坐斷千差萬別，頓超十地三賢，處處通方，頭頭得妙，致君堯舜上，再使風俗淳，鳳舞鸞翔，河清海晏。正當恁麼時如何？殊方喜見梯山貢，四野欣聞擊壤歌。復舉保壽開堂，三聖推出一僧，保壽便打公案，師拈云：二大老似鶻拏鳩、如鷹搦兔，收來放去，足有可觀。子細點撿將來，未免俱借這僧鼻孔出氣。若要扶竪臨濟正宗，且緩緩。當晚，小參。一水護田將綠遶，激揚少室家風；萬山排闥送青來，漏泄威音消息。恁麼會得，釋迦不出世，達磨不西來，佛法遍天下，談禪口不開，何必高推臨濟喝似雷奔，獨羨德山棒如雨點？人人脚跟下十日炳煥，箇箇肉髻中百寶光明，無邊剎境靡不流輝，十世古今舉無遺照。日月有顯晦，此則未嘗有顯晦；天地有盈虧，此則未嘗有盈虧。不離當處常湛然，覓則知君不可見。所以道：目前無法，意在目前；不是目前法，非耳目之所到。雖則非耳目之所到，爭柰意在目前？雖則意在目前，爭柰非耳目之所到？這裏一咬咬斷、一󳬇󳬇透，便見夾山眼睛、鼻孔元是自家鼻孔、眼睛。其或未然，莫道西江風浪惡，錢塘更有海門潮。復舉：南泉示眾云：王老師自小牧一頭水牯牛公案。師拈云：馬師道：惟有普願獨超物外。因甚自牧一頭水牯牛？莫擬如何頓放。且道過在什麼處？有人辨得，許你親見南泉。洪首座至，上堂：經誦三千部，曹溪一句忘；塵塵皆寶所，處處是家鄉。雲淨天如洗，潭清月愈光；須知遠煙浪，別有好商量。上堂，召大眾云：直下是，直下是，這邊那邊，滿眼滿耳，綿綿兮長存，湛湛兮不痕，擬議依前隔海門。上堂：雨滴空階，溪流新漲。風起天末，葉墜疎林。喚作物却非物，喚作心不是心。缺齒老胡會不得，九年面壁空沉吟。請後堂并義糓掌會，上堂。摩訶衍法，離四句，絕百非；香飯普熏，遍十方，窮三際。我此一眾總是諸方羅籠不住底，且道為法來耶？為飯來耶？良久，云：莫鈍置。開爐，上堂。竪拂子，召大眾云：這箇如大火聚，近之則燎却面門，是汝諸人如何湊泊？若也湊泊得去，盛夏不熱，嚴冬不寒；其或未然，終日雖在火爐頭，未免總是凍殺底數。上堂，召大眾云：佛法只在日用，日用百發百中。只如諸

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 不離當處常湛然，覓則知君不可見

Senses.Explanation: It never leaves this place and stays clear; seek it and you will not see it joins immediate presence to the failure of searching for it as an object. Poshan asks where a person now stands, strikes with his staff, and gives the pair. Gulin gives it after asking where a deceased lama is. Feiyin offers it as the line for setting foot on the present ground. Baichi gives it after asking his assembly if they recognize where the matter rests. Lianfeng uses it in a memorial address to say that the departed person need not be sought far away. Huanxi pairs it with a saying about what lies before the eyes yet is not reached through eye or ear alone.

Entries.SourceTerm: 不離當處常湛然，覓即知君不可見

Senses.PreferredTarget: Never apart from this very place, it remains clear and still; seek it, and you will know it cannot be seen
AlternateTargets: It is always lucid right here; when you search for it, you find it cannot be seen
SearchAliases: always clear here yet unseen when sought
not apart from here cannot be seen by seeking
Senses.Note: Yongjia says that the matter is never separate from this very place and remains clear and still; yet searching for it does not make it visible. Later masters use the pair at a funeral, after striking a staff or whisk, and in live answers about a true body or an unborn realm. Ruibai and Shenfeng explicitly identify the older verse and interpret it. The tension prevents both a remote search and a claim to possess a thing right here.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB188.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Rujiu Ruibai. Asked at a tea gathering for a shortcut into the Way, Ruibai recounts his own course of practice. After his teacher's questions exposed his difficulty, he stood before the Buddha for seven days and nights at Yanqing monastery. These two lines from the Song of Realization suddenly arose in him, and he says he awakened to himself. He calls this obtaining the root but immediately adds that he could not yet turn freely or understand other cases; further practice and later openings follow. Yongjia is the quoted verse voice, while Ruibai is the autobiographical narrator. The lines mark a specific opening, not the end of the entire account.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB184.xml). Seven-Session Recorded Sayings of Monk Muyun. This is Muyun's torch address for the deceased monk Zhaozhan, one of five separately headed funeral units. He first asks about neither coming nor going, with eyebrows and eyes continually facing one another, and asks the assembly what person this is. Sweeping the torch, he urges them to bring fire to the face and look, then gives the couplet. The action and address make it a present funeral instruction about what is not found by outward searching; the next unit for Ziran is a different deceased monk. Zhaozhan is the person commemorated, not the speaker of the verse.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB243.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Er’an Song. At a tea talk, Er'an answers a monk's questions about the message before speech and the final phrase; the monk shouts and Er'an responds with spring and flower-drum imagery. He then draws a circle with his staff and says the Buddha's true body is like empty space, appearing in response to things like the moon in water. Asking whether anyone has the eye to see, he concludes with the couplet. These are Er'an's own words in the present talk. The circle and question prepare the headword's warning against seeking a separate visible object; the following release-of-retreat address is another unit.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB249.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Fangrongxi. After questions on the three mysteries and essentials, Fangrong raises his whisk and sets those exchanges aside: do they understand this? He supplies a verse about one firm body appearing throughout the dusts and imagines the Buddhas unanimously telling the assembly not to leave 'this' in walking, standing, sitting, or lying down. He then asks what 'this' is called, drops the whisk, and gives the headword. The couplet answers his own present challenge without naming a separate object for pursuit. The next address, requested by a laywoman, is a new occasion.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J33/J33nB286.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yingningjing. Yingning first recounts Ouyang's conversation with a mountain monk, who explains that steadiness at death requires continual concentration and wisdom rather than continual distraction. Returning to his assembly, Yingning warns that indecision, disputes about self and others, and following circumstances leave one unprepared. He says the light has never been left from birth onward, but insists that saying so is not enough and urges timely effort. Striking his ceremonial scepter, he concludes with the couplet. The words are his present admonition following the reported conversation, not the old monk's answer to Ouyang.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB298.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shenfeng Xian. In a birthday address Shenfeng urges recognition before one's eyes rather than seeking outside the mind, then explicitly quotes Yongjia: the couplet is followed by 'It cannot be taken; it cannot be discarded; within the unobtainable, just thus obtain it.' Shenfeng asks how obtaining within the unobtainable is possible, strikes his staff, and lists its realization by Buddhas, people, and all beings. He then asks what he himself will do today and concludes with striking festive imagery and another staff action. Yongjia supplies the quoted verse; Shenfeng owns the probing question and subsequent deployment.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J35/J35nB342.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shengke (Huayan). A monk asks Shengke how not to violate either side of the alternatives of the Buddha speaking or not speaking and Kasyapa hearing or not hearing. Shengke first says he cannot state it here, then tests the monk's answering shout. In his address he brings the ancient assembly into the present, asks each person to turn back and examine, and says the Buddha and Kasyapa are not separate from those present. He then restores the actual difference: he returns to his quarters and the assembly to their places. The headword answers his final 'What then?' It is Shengke's current conclusion, not a quotation spoken by the historical Buddha.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB359.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baiyu. In an address occasioned by the season, Baiyu strikes his whisk and asks what time this is. He groups Xiangyan's bamboo sound, Lingyun's peach blossoms, Dongshan's reflection, Xuansha's injured toe, and awakening through sights or sounds as occasions not apart from this time. He then asks how it is when one does not fall into conditioned occasions and times. Striking the whisk again, he gives the couplet. Its local role is to answer that last question, rather than to claim that every seasonal or sensory event is already an awakening. The following visit to Luan is a separate address.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB364.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Foguwen. In a short address before the deceased's spirit, Fogu describes what birth and death do not reach and contrasts letting go with holding fast. Images of a moon in a clear pool and a bell in the still night suggest responding without loss, but he explicitly says that, examined closely, this is still not the realm of nonarising. He asks what that realm is, strikes his staff, and gives the couplet. The headword is his response beyond the preceding attractive descriptions; the note does not equate those descriptions with the answer he has just withheld. The subsequent ordination address is another occasion.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB188.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Rujiu Ruibai. Asked at a tea gathering for a shortcut into the Way, Ruibai recounts his own course of practice. After his teacher's questions exposed his difficulty, he stood before the Buddha for seven days and nights at Yanqing monastery. These two lines from the Song of Realization suddenly arose in him, and he says he awakened to himself. He calls this obtaining the root but immediately adds that he could not yet turn freely or understand other cases; further practice and later openings follow. Yongjia is the quoted verse voice, while Ruibai is the autobiographical narrator. The lines mark a specific opening, not the end of the entire account.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB184.xml). Seven-Session Recorded Sayings of Monk Muyun. This is Muyun's torch address for the deceased monk Zhaozhan, one of five separately headed funeral units. He first asks about neither coming nor going, with eyebrows and eyes continually facing one another, and asks the assembly what person this is. Sweeping the torch, he urges them to bring fire to the face and look, then gives the couplet. The action and address make it a present funeral instruction about what is not found by outward searching; the next unit for Ziran is a different deceased monk. Zhaozhan is the person commemorated, not the speaker of the verse.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB243.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Er’an Song. At a tea talk, Er'an answers a monk's questions about the message before speech and the final phrase; the monk shouts and Er'an responds with spring and flower-drum imagery. He then draws a circle with his staff and says the Buddha's true body is like empty space, appearing in response to things like the moon in water. Asking whether anyone has the eye to see, he concludes with the couplet. These are Er'an's own words in the present talk. The circle and question prepare the headword's warning against seeking a separate visible object; the following release-of-retreat address is another unit.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB249.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Fangrongxi. After questions on the three mysteries and essentials, Fangrong raises his whisk and sets those exchanges aside: do they understand this? He supplies a verse about one firm body appearing throughout the dusts and imagines the Buddhas unanimously telling the assembly not to leave 'this' in walking, standing, sitting, or lying down. He then asks what 'this' is called, drops the whisk, and gives the headword. The couplet answers his own present challenge without naming a separate object for pursuit. The next address, requested by a laywoman, is a new occasion.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 、毛栗如彈塞卻喉。果能裂出神龍之首，則佛祖不能安汝名、天魔不能窺汝蹟。勿則浪沉往返，杳喪光陰。昔歐陽文忘公官洛中，一日游嵩山，卻去僕吏，放意而往。至山寺，修竹滿軒，霜清烏啼。文忠休於殿陛，旁有老僧閱經自若，與語不甚顧答。公異之，問曰：『道人住山久如？』對曰：『甚久也。』又問：『誦何經？』對曰：『《法華》。』公曰：『古之高僧，臨生死之際，類皆談笑脫去，何道致之耶？』對曰：『定慧力耳。』又問：『今乃寂寥無有，何哉？』老僧笑曰：『古之人念念在定慧，臨終安得亂？今之人念念在散亂，臨終安得定？』文忠大喜，不知膝之屈地。」師云：「你看學道者，不是徒然泛泛，未能決其志，終日在人我山中打迸、是非場裡橫身，他時如何抵敵？蓋疑信相半，因而隨情逐物，臨窮方悔，噬臍何及？特此告報。須知出母胎，從少至老，盡未來際，未曾離卻這個光明。果能一腳踏穿桶底，何處有死生之所流轉？但不是說了便休，今且乘風快便，莫令失卻時日。蕺山恁地熱亂，還識好惡否？」擊如意，云：「不離當處常湛然，覓即知君不可見。」解制，知浴設茶請示眾。「露柱當天豁雙眼，未為奇特；蟭螟怒發吞大象，理亦宜然。果是伶俐衲僧，便可一捺便倒。若隨人緇素得來，總是倚草附木漢。過在紅線未斷，撥著好似浪裏拋毬，徒費草鞋錢，堪作何用？上智之士一聞釋然，中下之流疑而愈滯。蕺山與麼道，自好慚惶煞人。」復舉：「昔有一官人入寺至禪堂，寺主隨行，官人問曰：『諸位在此作麼生？』對曰：『欲圖作佛。』官人笑云：『金屑雖貴，落眼成翳。』主無語。」師乃云：「好笑寺主恁不唧溜，被俗漢一問，直得口如扁擔。若遇蕺山，但向他道：『在此換居士眼睛。』非唯令俗漢屏卻咽喉，亦見此中凜然難犯。諸仁者應知：有佛處不得住，無佛處急走過。轉得快，便不負蕺山和身一拶；如或未然，明年更有新條在，惱亂春風卒未休。」修萬佛懺圓期，上堂。師陞座。學人問：「古鏡未磨時，光臨萬象。磨後為甚麼不鑑？」師云：「我卻不識你。」進云：「恁麼則是處是彌勒，無門無善財。」師云：「猶借玉階行。」進云：「如是則學人別道去也。」以手點空三下，便作禮，師云：「料掉沒交涉。」師乃云：「香花雲，寶幢雲，乾闥婆王美樂音，出生無盡諸功德，裂破三賢十地門。雲從龍，風從虎，磁石吸針潮長醋，情與無情共一真，萬象森羅鏡裏布。如是知，如是住，不見一法為伴侶
ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J33/J33nB286.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yingningjing. Yingning first recounts Ouyang's conversation with a mountain monk, who explains that steadiness at death requires continual concentration and wisdom rather than continual distraction. Returning to his assembly, Yingning warns that indecision, disputes about self and others, and following circumstances leave one unprepared. He says the light has never been left from birth onward, but insists that saying so is not enough and urges timely effort. Striking his ceremonial scepter, he concludes with the couplet. The words are his present admonition following the reported conversation, not the old monk's answer to Ouyang.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB298.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shenfeng Xian. In a birthday address Shenfeng urges recognition before one's eyes rather than seeking outside the mind, then explicitly quotes Yongjia: the couplet is followed by 'It cannot be taken; it cannot be discarded; within the unobtainable, just thus obtain it.' Shenfeng asks how obtaining within the unobtainable is possible, strikes his staff, and lists its realization by Buddhas, people, and all beings. He then asks what he himself will do today and concludes with striking festive imagery and another staff action. Yongjia supplies the quoted verse; Shenfeng owns the probing question and subsequent deployment.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J35/J35nB342.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shengke (Huayan). A monk asks Shengke how not to violate either side of the alternatives of the Buddha speaking or not speaking and Kasyapa hearing or not hearing. Shengke first says he cannot state it here, then tests the monk's answering shout. In his address he brings the ancient assembly into the present, asks each person to turn back and examine, and says the Buddha and Kasyapa are not separate from those present. He then restores the actual difference: he returns to his quarters and the assembly to their places. The headword answers his final 'What then?' It is Shengke's current conclusion, not a quotation spoken by the historical Buddha.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB364.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Foguwen. In a short address before the deceased's spirit, Fogu describes what birth and death do not reach and contrasts letting go with holding fast. Images of a moon in a clear pool and a bell in the still night suggest responding without loss, but he explicitly says that, examined closely, this is still not the realm of nonarising. He asks what that realm is, strikes his staff, and gives the couplet. The headword is his response beyond the preceding attractive descriptions; the note does not equate those descriptions with the answer he has just withheld. The subsequent ordination address is another occasion.

Senses.Explanation: The couplet says that what is being sought remains clear and still without leaving this very place, yet becomes unavailable to sight through the act of seeking it. 'This place' is the present situation, not an instruction to travel to a special location. The retained passages often join the words to an action: drawing a circle, raising or dropping a whisk, striking a staff, or moving a funeral torch. Those actions belong to particular speakers and occasions, rather than serving as a single code for the phrase. Ruibai recalls the lines of Yongjia's Song of Realization arising during his practice and distinguishes that opening from later work. Shenfeng explicitly quotes Yongjia and asks how 'obtaining' is possible within what cannot be obtained. Other masters use the couplet as their own concluding answer to a present question about the body of the Buddha, birth and death, or the relation between an awakening occasion and what does not depend on such conditions.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X68/X68n1319.xml). Imperially Selected Recorded Sayings. This record says Dongshan received the Precious Mirror teaching from Yunyan and now gives it to Caoshan, then recites its words. Near the end, minister serving ruler and child following father introduce the headword's warning that failing these duties is neither filial nor supportive. It leads into hidden, continuous activity compared to foolishness. Dongshan is therefore the reported reciter in this scene; receipt and transmission do not prove that he individually composed the text. The pair works within its images of reciprocal positions, while the following instructions also warn Caoshan about several kinds of leaking understanding.

Occurrences.Kwic: 士又問五位王子，師乃云：「臣奉于君，子順于父，不順非孝，不奉非輔。作麼生說個孝的道理？但一切處自然莫教觸犯、莫教違逆，件件到恰好田地，這是子職之所當盡。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J33/J33nB294.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Liangting Ting of Yunxi. Asked by the layman Jianmei about the five ranks of princes, Liangting Jingting voices the minister-and-child lines and asks what filial conduct means. One should naturally avoid conflict and deviation and meet each matter appropriately, he says, then explains ruler and father as the honored position and minister and child as the position that supports it. He distinguishes types of prince and criticizes people who discuss these ranks without knowing their source. The headword is his present explanatory revoicing, not a new biographical command to one particular child or a sufficient substitute for understanding the Chan scheme.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB190.xml). Dharma Platform of Chan Master Shiyu. In his offering for the deceased Jinian, keeper of the retreat cell, Shiyu Mingfang presents incense and water, then asks whether the deceased supplies him or he supplies the deceased. A life of clear up-and-down relations has now put head where tail was; why is this so? After a pause he gives the headword. The inherited language of child and minister caps a ritual reversal of the expected giver and receiver. The brief source does not specify an ordinary family dispute, a biological father-son relationship or a political act of disobedience, so those should not be invented to explain the funeral turn.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB298.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shenfeng Xian. Shenfeng Xian sets the Buddha's birth beside Yunmen's proposed blow. He calls the birth an unnecessary occasion for trouble; at the blow he gives the filial-and-supportive pair and says only then is Yunmen seen. The formula is Shenfeng's current cap, applying the language of serving and following to a gesture that superficially attacks the Buddha. Its local provocation asks how a hard corrective response can belong to genuine continuity. It is not a report that Yunmen historically struck the newborn Buddha, nor does this terse comparison justify arbitrary violence as obedience.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB408.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Aziwa of Haichuang. At a birthday address arranged by Danxia for the elder teacher, Azi Jinwu praises longevity through pine, snow, mountains and ancient figures, yet says even splendid wishes cannot exhaust what is honored. He cites the received Mirror-text sequence about minister, ruler, child and father, then strikes his staff and places its age alongside the ancient great tree, without needing a golden casting. The exact headword is a textual quotation whose individual composer is not identified by this turn. Azi's present birthday offering and staff gesture give it its local function; no unsupported original authorship should be assigned to the guest or commentator.

Senses.Explanation: The death-flinging stance Chan rows demand before the thinking mind can step in. Guting Shanjian, instructing his trainee, rules that knowing life-and-death to be this perilous, one must through all twelve hours disregard danger and death, cast body and life away, and see the matter through to a verdict; Yingshan Zhiyin, on the dragon-boat festival, grants that even the tide-players fling peril aside and smash their cauldrons, then asks how much more the great matter of life and death deserves it; Hanyue Fazang gives the portrait of one who does — a mallet to the mouth before the question, front teeth on the ground, a sword at the brow, blood spattering the Brahma heaven; and Wuyi Yuanlai, at the same festival, sets the pearl under the dragon's jaw and rules it must be snatched heedless of danger before a hand can land on it. Lianyue Daozheng lets Yangqi's three-legged donkey tread down Xuanzha's tiger and asks who, not heeding danger and death, will save it, snapping that the sweet melon is sweet to the stem; Lianfeng Su's elite striver drills bone for marrow atop Vairocana's crown, slices flesh to blow on the hair at the master's heel, enters with a single blade, and becomes blind-donkey seed; Zhufeng Zhenxu, enthroned at the old man's call, claims the stance for himself — heedless of danger and death he opens the alms-bowl there and raises the Tiantong principle and the Zhaojue gate; and Liao'an Qingyu conjures just such a reckless fellow bursting out to rule that his own Benjue verdict also deserves the twenty staves, ordering the incense attendant to arrange it.

Entries.SourceTerm: 對境心數起，菩提作麼長

Senses.PreferredTarget: In the face of things, thoughts keep arising; how could awakening grow?
AlternateTargets: Facing circumstances, the mind repeatedly stirs; how could awakening be made to grow?
SearchAliases: thoughts arise on meeting things how could awakening grow
Senses.Note: The local exchange governs each application; uncertain imagery and memorial claims are kept qualified.

Occurrences.Kwic: 復舉：「臥輪禪師偈云：『臥輪有伎倆，能斷百思想，對境心不起，菩提日日長。』六祖大師偈云：『慧能沒伎倆，不斷百思想，對境心數起，菩提作麼長？』大眾！臥輪不善用心，大似無繩自縛。六祖雖是對病說方，其奈以五十步笑百步。黃巖即不然，陸地千波涌，長江一滴無。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB208.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Guxue Zhe. Guxue Zhenzhe raises Wolun's verse claiming skill in stopping thoughts so the mind does not arise before objects and awakening grows daily. Huineng's answering verse denies such skill: thoughts are not cut off, mind repeatedly arises before objects, so how could awakening grow? Guxue calls Wolun self-bound without a rope, but says Huineng's medicine for that illness still resembles someone retreating fifty paces laughing at someone retreating a hundred. His own cap gives waves surging on dry land and not a drop in the long river. The exact question remains Huineng's quoted reversal; Guxue also refuses to let that reversal become the final formula.

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉：「慧能大師會下有僧，嘗舉臥輪禪師偈曰：『臥輪有伎倆，能斷百思想。對境心不起，菩提日月長。』祖聞之曰：『此偈未明心地，若依而行之，是加繫縛。』因示偈曰：『慧能沒伎倆，不斷百思想。對境心數起，菩提作麼長？』山僧亦有偈曰：『行謐閑伎倆，千思與萬想。隨起即隨滅，誰滅復誰長？』眾兄弟，且道那裏是明心地處？那裏是加繫縛處？試撿點看。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB212.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Eryin Mi. Eryin Mi recounts a monk presenting Wolun's thought-stopping verse to Huineng. Huineng calls it a failure to understand the mind-ground which adds bondage if followed, then offers the counterverse asking how awakening could grow when mind repeatedly arises before objects. Eryin adds his own verse: thoughts arise and cease, but who ceases and who grows? He asks the assembly to examine where understanding lies and where bondage is added. Huineng is the quoted speaker of the headword; Eryin's added questions bring the apparent opposition between stopping and allowing thoughts back under present examination.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB244.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Sanshanlai. In an instruction to secretary Xing, Sanshan Denglai praises steadfast practice through illness and ordinary service. At first, circumstances refine the mind; with maturity neither circumstances nor mind need be forcibly removed. He sets Wolun's verse of stopping thoughts beside Huineng's question about awakening's growth. Unlike a simple dismissal of Wolun, Sanshan calls the former effective cultivation and the latter overturning the barrier, then insists that effective cultivation is needed before that overturning. The headword is Huineng's quoted question within Sanshan's account of development, not permission to replace sustained work with a slogan of having no techniques.

Occurrences.Kwic: 祖亦不當教人云：『佛法在世間，不離世間覺；離世覓菩提，恰如求兔角。』又不當云：『對境心數起，菩提作麼長？』真正是個宗門中兒孫，絕不別引前人舊唾，使人釘樁搖櫓。故曰：男兒自有沖霄翅，不向他人行處行。總之，未徹目前境界，便不知自己通身是？遍身是？取之左右無不是，所以不能當軒舉起，令人直下信得。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J40/J40nB478.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yan Jushen of Yunshan. In conversation with Yan, Yanju Deshen challenges a teaching that seeks mind apart from circumstances. Asked about Huineng's instruction to still conditions and not produce a thought, he distinguishes settling from separation: a wave settling into water remains inseparable from it. If Huineng required abandoning circumstances, Yanju argues, he could not also have taught awakening within the world or asked how awakening grows while mind repeatedly arises before objects. The headword is Huineng's quoted evidence in this argument. Yanju's polemic does not authorize treating his description of rival teachings as a neutral account of their own views, nor turn settling into mere indifference to circumstances.

Senses.Explanation: The sovereign's second pressing of the first ancestor — who is it that faces me? — raised, retold, oded, and answered on his behalf across the records. Wuzu Fayan raises the exchange at his evening teaching and throws it against Huineng — the Sixth Ancestor, asked who won Huangmei's purport, answered only that those who know the teaching won it and that he himself did not know the teaching — great and small ancestors, pressed, all not-knowing and not-understanding: why then grandchildren everywhere?; Zhongfeng Mingben picks up the case with the gap-toothed old monk's mud pellets, out to out-rich the eastern lands — and the Liang sovereign points the light-giving pearl at him, so he can only say he does not know; Hengchuan Rugong takes it into his own ode — vast and no sage, a true saying; who faces me? the heart not yet at rest — the original light shining through the ten directions from measureless ears to today; and Shiyu Mingfang grades the press itself: the sovereign's blood-seeing hand squeezed one more asking, and not-knowing, not-knowing, good as it is, saves only half — the river crossing and nine years of wall-facing cannot save the other, and the arm-severing Huike and the six generations and five houses have been holding up that other half ever since. Poshan Haiming tells it as the first ancestor's own errand — seeing great-vehicle roots in this land, crossing the sea to meet an emperor who loved the teaching and took the highest meaning for the ultimate — and the not-knowing that broke the meeting, the reed crossed, the wall faced; Fushi Tongxian turns it on the hearers: some, hearing it raised, force themselves into mastery — no cudgel turns them, no snare holds them, a stone guardian at the crossroads, nothing but a blockhead — while the true man keeps the idle ground all year, no sages above to long for, no beings below to save; Minshu Ruxiang rules the emperor eyed but did not see the cheek behind, the ancestor's words rang but hid their edge, the middle way open one thread and the sovereign missed it face to face — the empire can be shared out, ranks resigned, bare blades walked, the middle cannot be done; and Jifei Ruyi, picking up the case, finds the Liang sovereign meeting yet not meeting and the first ancestor knowing yet not knowing — two faceless fellows — with knowing the no-sage vastness the sole honor under heaven.

Senses.PreferredTarget: respond to the occasion
AlternateTargets: meet the occasion
occasion-matching exchange
Senses.Explanation: Literally, to face or match the occasion. In Chan records it names responsive encounter rather than a private state. One early lamp compilation makes “encounters responding to the occasion” a section heading for recorded cases. A later questioner says that during “questioning and discrimination in responding to the occasion” his responses are not free-flowing, and asks where the fault lies; Zhanran Yuancheng's answer examines him rather than treating interview performance as optional. A recorded dialogue asks where the three vehicles and twelve divisions of teaching were obtained, and Muzhou Daoming answers, “they were obtained in responding to the occasion.” Hongzhi speaks of “an eye for responding to the occasion in engaging the world,” followed by the claim that the many conditions cannot bury it. The same verb extends to audience-responsive speech: Gu Xue records that those of sharp capacity are told to investigate Chan and those of middling or lower capacity to invoke buddha, calling this “speaking in response to the occasion,” then asks what is right or wrong. The corpus also uses the term in titles such as collections of hundreds of encounters, in appraisals of the respondent's answer, and in compounds with answering and reception. Thus the ordinary graph “occasion” or “capacity” (機) is bent toward the live occasion or capacity presented by another: “respond to the occasion” (對機) means meeting it in an answer, action, exchange, or address preserved by the record.
Senses.Note: “Occasion” keeps the range of the graph “occasion/capacity” (機) without importing a mystical faculty. The heading, question-and-discrimination phrase, direct answer, and “eye” collocation all require an interpersonal responsive sense. Compare “meet the occasion”, “occasion of encounter”, “question-and-answer”, and “responsive engagement”; none is simply synonymous.

Entries.SourceTerm: 對面不相識，千里卻同風

Senses.PreferredTarget: Face to face, they do not recognize each other; a thousand miles apart, they share the same wind.
AlternateTargets: Unrecognized at close range, yet of one current across a thousand miles.
SearchAliases: face to face not recognize thousand miles same wind Chan
unrecognized nearby one current far away Zen
Senses.Note: Wuyi voices the pair in his own position teaching; Tianan applies it to a shared course; Yikui follows it by asking who truly shares the wind; Hanke opens his own case verse with it. An earlier Wuyi gloss uses the same pair between quoted lines of his Shouchang teachers verse, but that second occurrence is not counted as an independent work. In these present uses, recognizing someone by ordinary sight and sharing a course are deliberately held apart.

Occurrences.Kwic: 制，又是半月了也。諸昆仲！分上曾有個入處也無？若無箇入處，須要尋個入處；若得個入處，須要尋個出處。直須自看。諸昆仲！當知：古路無塵，只須知有門庭，絕待盡卻。今時偏方與正位攸同，枝派共靈源皎潔，到此則髑髏識盡、烈火流金始名出世，更須知有野老家風始得。且道：野老家風是何景象？」卓拄杖，云：「遲日穿芳逕，春鋤帶雨歸。」下座。上堂。僧問：「古人道：『從緣薦得相應疾，就體消停得力遲。』請問：如何是從緣薦得？」師云：「古鏡不重磨。」進云：「如何是就體消停？」師云：「清光仍似舊。」進云：「從緣就體蒙師指，格外玄談有也無？」師云：「三歲孩兒頭似雪。」進云：「恁麼則碧桃綻蕊、綠柳萌芽也。」師云：「遠觀山有色，近聽水無聲。」僧禮拜，師乃云：「切忌從他覓，迢迢與我疏。洞山老人草鞋斷矣、腳跟露矣，諸人若知痛癢，阿誰皮下無血？博山與諸人同途不同轍，諸人向正位中來，博山不在正位，諸人在博山拂子裏許；諸人向偏位中來，博山不在偏位，拂子在諸人袈裟裏許。所以道：對面不相識，千里卻同風。若向這裏徹去，當下知歸，不留朕兆；其或未然，千百世修行未為晚也。故我釋迦大師為勇猛眾生成佛在一念頃，為懈怠眾生得果滿僧祗劫。諸昆仲！當知明中有暗，毫端現華藏之奇妙，挾協通寶鏡，瀉山河之影。博山恁麼道，猶是葛藤，諸人也須拼斷始得。且道：拼斷後作麼生行履？」卓拄杖，云：「不因樵子逕，爭到葛洪家？」結制，上堂。僧問：「古人道：『塵中能作主，化外自來賓。』請問：如何是塵中主？」師云：「江西原是豫章城。」進云：「如何是化外賓？」師云：「青山自青山。」進云：「賓主相見時如何？」師云：「綠水忻綠水。」進云：「恁麼則金繩界畔飄黃葉，般若堂前解垢衣，一句作麼生道？」師云：「順數一籌。」進云：「博山今日結制，人人鼻孔撩天，請問更與諸人說箇甚麼？」師云：「空中施彩繪，論劫不成顏。」僧禮拜，師乃云：「便恁麼進堂去，猶較些子，更欲遲疑，劍去久矣。博山從來無佛法繫綴於人，豈但博山？乃至諸佛諸祖亦復如是，但有言說，都無實義。所以道：釋迦不達南方禪，達磨不會西來意。博山與諸人秪知二時逐隊，但恁麼過時。臨濟三玄三要，誑嚇小兒；曹洞兼帶協通，顢頇無識；溈仰暗機圓合，鬼面神頭；雲門函蓋乾坤，心麤膽大；法眼雖云平易，機險殺人。博山總不恁麼，今日與諸昆仲結制，將九
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB197.xml). Recorded sayings. Wuyi voices the pair in his own sermon on the relative and correct positions.

Occurrences.Kwic: 道吾舞笏、秘魔擎叉、禾山打鼓、雪峰輥毬，八佾舞于庭。殊不知君子務本，本立而道生。故林放問禮之本，子曰：『大哉問。』然則如何是禮之本？心王不妄動，六國一時通，罷拈三尺劍，休弄一張弓。但見皇風成一片，不知何處有隅封？」喝一喝。解制，秉拂。「雪色初晴，春山澹蕩，桃腮未滴胭脂雨，梅萼先招玉蝶風。憶歸期，數歸期，別時容易見時稀，杜鵑枝上啼。長相思，短相思，從前客夢已如癡，喚回知幾時？諸兄弟！同堂共住以來又是一期了也，昇上座自愧不才，終日絮絮叨叨，不是為你破除妄見，便是為你剷削情根。你欲住卻不許你住，用錐錐你，用錐錐你也，移華兼蝶至；你欲去又不許你去，用鉤鉤你，用鉤鉤你也，買石得雲饒。正當恁麼時，欲住未住、欲去未去，鉤錐齊歇，兩手分付。兩手分付也，分明月在梅華上，看到梅華早已遲。所以此事不在久參、不在初學，直須立地搆去。果然立地搆去，則何妨跨楊岐三腳之驢，朝遊天台、暮遊南嶽；解彌勒布袋之口，橫臥華街，倒穿柳巷？何故？此人通途合轍，事同一家，對面不相識，千里卻同風。其或未然，相思相見知何日？淚落珊瑚正未休。」秉拂。問：「風搖雪萼家家月，雲漾華魂色色光，珍重陽春回足下，特呈舊面發清香。為復是師資契合？為復是啐啄同時？」師云：「隨人卜度。」進云：「恁麼則龍向洞中銜雨出，鳥從華裏帶香飛。」師云：「不動如來在什麼處？」進云：「祇如正當解制之節，臨行一句又且如何？」師云：「日中有烏，月中有兔。」進云：「學人又不然。」師云：「你試呈朦袋看。」進云：「鵬飛天外千重影，鯤向南溟萬派波。」師云：「瓊華觀裏鐵師子。」乃云：「五里一箇亭，十里一箇舖，雲水去趨蹌，盡蹋來時路。翠嵒啜齒粘牙、趙州捏鼻呷醋，一箇落盡眉毛、一箇老無住處，那知灑脫衲僧，腳下絕無迴互？雖無迴互，莫忘名顧，一句臨行平等分付，日中有烏，月中有兔。」擊拂子，下座。萬善殿，秉拂。「萬仞崖前冰雪封，嬾僧高臥覓無蹤，何緣歸省玲瓏畔？一櫂風吹到帝宮。皇風蕩蕩，南北宗通，同堂相聚，略展家風。不見道：雲月是同，谿山各異。還有解得無舌人語者，不妨出眾相見。」良久，眾不出，乃云：「此事不在多言，言多去道轉遠。諸公既知時節，昇上座亦說箇應時及節底說話，與諸公醒醒瞌睡。得一萬事畢，衲僧難辦別竿木。既隨身潦倒，為君說一元和、二達磨、三碗脫丘，千峰勢到嶽邊止，知止
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB187.xml). Recorded sayings. Tianan voices the pair in his own sermon on shared course and immediate recognition.

Occurrences.Kwic: 葉騰芳歲月長。」清明，上堂。「鶯梭日逐大忙生，織就天機錦繡春，何事佳人不解惜？遍尋芳艸哭新墳。好傷心，不傷心，將謂眾生苦，更有苦眾生。大眾且道：如何免得？」卓拄杖，云：「莫待老來方學道，新墳多是少年人。」晚參。「三春已盡，夏景斯臨，香嚴擊開漆桶，靈雲打失眼睛，玄沙寂子據款結案，致令千古有屈難伸。且道屈如何伸？」眾無語，師云：「禍不入慎家之門。」佛誕，上堂。豎拂子，云：「纔見毘藍出頭，又向雙林縮頭，詎料百千年後撞著韶陽對頭？爭如者裏罷卻干戈百艸頭，夜來明月落溪頭，便見戴角擎頭、鐵額銅頭、普天匝地、法法頭頭，若喚作佛，頭上安頭。畢竟如何？總為戰征收拾得，卻因歌舞破除休。」瑞巖先老人週忌，拈香。「去年今日一段義，青天白日人誰識？今朝對面不相逢，蓋色騎聲秪者是。」師誕日，上堂。「淨法界身，本無出沒。三世凍儂，歷代開士。甚麼物恁麼來？大悲願力，示現受生，救得眉毛完全。者幾箇？無生猶是末，何況有生？到者裏，諸天散花無路，鬼神窺覷無門。雖然，對面不相識，千里卻同風。誰是同風者？眼卓朔，頭髼鬆。」端午，上堂。「五月五，懸艾虎，驅百病，蕩邪路。昨日有人從天台來，卻得南嶽信報道：湖南境內，瘟㾮所司，得乘其便，人民死者不可稱可。符使不靈，執蒲劍，跨艾虎，倒退三千，卻來問云：『此山得保無虞者，不審修何行？習何業？用何玅術？』山僧笑而不答。木上座在傍忍俊不禁，云：『家無白澤之圖，必無如是妖怪。』山僧驀口一摑，不覺吐舌。大眾！還知落處麼？疑則禍生。」自修禪人請上堂。問：「鐘聲纔動，請法殷勤，大眾雲臻，如何指示？」師云：「曲不藏直。」進云：「未明心地法，難過趙州關。如何是趙州關？」師云：「十字縱橫。」進云：「一堂風冷淡，千古意分明。」師云：「切忌訛言。」乃云：「當陽一著，迥絕遮攔，不屬盈虧，若為修證？修證不無染污，不得腦門著楔也。如牛駕車，打車打牛，四稜踏地也。所以，五千餘卷無非黃葉止啼，八萬四千法門總是繫驢橛子，須是獨超物外、生鐵鑄成底，乃能不重己靈、不慕諸聖，奴呼菩薩、婢視聲聞，然後興無緣慈、作不請友，運出自己家珍，大作金牛佛事。正當因齋慶讚，又且如何話會？木札羹與鐵釘飯，不是飽餐人不知。」弘覺忞師翁忌日，拈香。「棄儒冠而喜緇衣之宜，究產難因緣而撞彩瞥地，何其居寰海而赫赫聲馳，入皇宮而耽耽虎視？

Occurrences.Kwic: 一老人，問：「向甚處去？」者云：「臺山禮文殊去。」老人云：「大德！見文殊還識不？」者無對。師云：「當時若見恁麼道，但云：『祗如文殊，還識某甲也無？』」又云：「文殊！文殊。」頌曰：「文殊豈有二文殊？尋到臺山也大迂。昨夜雪晴雲破處，一鉤新月小空虛。」趙州問座主：「講甚麼經？」主云：「《涅槃經》。」州云：「問大德一段義得不？」主云：「問甚麼義？」州以腳趯空一趯，吹一吹，云：「者個是什麼義？」主云：「經中無此義。」州云：「脫空謾語漢。此是五百力士揭石義。」師云：「且道是此義？不是此義？座主若具眼，待渠問：『這個是甚麼義？』但向道：『少賣弄。』或云：『久知和尚有此機關。』不特勘破趙州，免令錯下註腳。」頌曰：「口裡無牙，腳底無筋。趙州老漢，少喜多嗔。」趙州問僧：「發足甚處？」僧云：「雪峰。」州云：「雪峰有何言句示人？」僧云：「尋常道：『盡十方世界是沙門一隻眼，你等諸人向甚處屙？』」州云：「闍黎若迴，寄個鍬子去。」師云：「彼彼相助。」頌曰：「對面不相識，千里卻同風。若無河北輪刀手，誰解幫扶老雪峰？」紫湖門下立牌，牌上書云：「紫湖有狗，上取人頭，中取人腰，下取人腳，擬議則喪身失命。」有新到纔相看，湖便喝云：「看狗。」僧纔回首，湖便歸方丈。師云：「紫湖可謂老婆心切，爭奈無人捨命？」李居士請師於看狗處下語，師直前一摑。又云：「幸是老僧。」又云：「業畜不得無禮。」又於地上作󵐘相，隨以腳抹卻，又以手舉腰帶云：「個是五百文買底。」頌曰：「紫湖一隻狗，牙長善抖擻。誰論跖與堯，彌勒遭一口。」睦州因秀才相看，云：「會二十四家書。」州以拄杖空中點一點，云：「會麼？」秀才罔措。州云：「又道會二十四家書，永字八法也不識。」師云：「睦州者一點，莫道秀才家，便是佛來也不敢正眼覷著。」又云：「如蟲禦木。」頌曰：「一點分明露，其如識字多。若將八法論，鷂子過新羅。」葉縣省禪師問僧云：「日暮投林，朝離何處？」僧云：「某甲不曾學禪。」師云：「生身入地獄。」師云：「且道是者僧入地獄，是葉縣入地獄？」頌曰：「學禪不學禪，蜂蜜比糖甜。生身入地獄，千足與萬足。」楚圓禪師冬日榜示，僧堂前作此相，若人識得，不離四威儀中。師云：「當時若見，脫草鞋蘸水向上一擦。」頌曰：「天皇皇，地皇皇，我家有個夜啼郎。往來君子讀一遍，安眠穩睡到天光。」

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 道吾舞笏、秘魔擎叉、禾山打鼓、雪峰輥毬，八佾舞于庭。殊不知君子務本，本立而道生。故林放問禮之本，子曰：『大哉問。』然則如何是禮之本？心王不妄動，六國一時通，罷拈三尺劍，休弄一張弓。但見皇風成一片，不知何處有隅封？」喝一喝。解制，秉拂。「雪色初晴，春山澹蕩，桃腮未滴胭脂雨，梅萼先招玉蝶風。憶歸期，數歸期，別時容易見時稀，杜鵑枝上啼。長相思，短相思，從前客夢已如癡，喚回知幾時？諸兄弟！同堂共住以來又是一期了也，昇上座自愧不才，終日絮絮叨叨，不是為你破除妄見，便是為你剷削情根。你欲住卻不許你住，用錐錐你，用錐錐你也，移華兼蝶至；你欲去又不許你去，用鉤鉤你，用鉤鉤你也，買石得雲饒。正當恁麼時，欲住未住、欲去未去，鉤錐齊歇，兩手分付。兩手分付也，分明月在梅華上，看到梅華早已遲。所以此事不在久參、不在初學，直須立地搆去。果然立地搆去，則何妨跨楊岐三腳之驢，朝遊天台、暮遊南嶽；解彌勒布袋之口，橫臥華街，倒穿柳巷？何故？此人通途合轍，事同一家，對面不相識，千里卻同風。其或未然，相思相見知何日？淚落珊瑚正未休。」秉拂。問：「風搖雪萼家家月，雲漾華魂色色光，珍重陽春回足下，特呈舊面發清香。為復是師資契合？為復是啐啄同時？」師云：「隨人卜度。」進云：「恁麼則龍向洞中銜雨出，鳥從華裏帶香飛。」師云：「不動如來在什麼處？」進云：「祇如正當解制之節，臨行一句又且如何？」師云：「日中有烏，月中有兔。」進云：「學人又不然。」師云：「你試呈朦袋看。」進云：「鵬飛天外千重影，鯤向南溟萬派波。」師云：「瓊華觀裏鐵師子。」乃云：「五里一箇亭，十里一箇舖，雲水去趨蹌，盡蹋來時路。翠嵒啜齒粘牙、趙州捏鼻呷醋，一箇落盡眉毛、一箇老無住處，那知灑脫衲僧，腳下絕無迴互？雖無迴互，莫忘名顧，一句臨行平等分付，日中有烏，月中有兔。」擊拂子，下座。萬善殿，秉拂。「萬仞崖前冰雪封，嬾僧高臥覓無蹤，何緣歸省玲瓏畔？一櫂風吹到帝宮。皇風蕩蕩，南北宗通，同堂相聚，略展家風。不見道：雲月是同，谿山各異。還有解得無舌人語者，不妨出眾相見。」良久，眾不出，乃云：「此事不在多言，言多去道轉遠。諸公既知時節，昇上座亦說箇應時及節底說話，與諸公醒醒瞌睡。得一萬事畢，衲僧難辦別竿木。既隨身潦倒，為君說一元和、二達磨、三碗脫丘，千峰勢到嶽邊止，知止

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 一老人，問：「向甚處去？」者云：「臺山禮文殊去。」老人云：「大德！見文殊還識不？」者無對。師云：「當時若見恁麼道，但云：『祗如文殊，還識某甲也無？』」又云：「文殊！文殊。」頌曰：「文殊豈有二文殊？尋到臺山也大迂。昨夜雪晴雲破處，一鉤新月小空虛。」趙州問座主：「講甚麼經？」主云：「《涅槃經》。」州云：「問大德一段義得不？」主云：「問甚麼義？」州以腳趯空一趯，吹一吹，云：「者個是什麼義？」主云：「經中無此義。」州云：「脫空謾語漢。此是五百力士揭石義。」師云：「且道是此義？不是此義？座主若具眼，待渠問：『這個是甚麼義？』但向道：『少賣弄。』或云：『久知和尚有此機關。』不特勘破趙州，免令錯下註腳。」頌曰：「口裡無牙，腳底無筋。趙州老漢，少喜多嗔。」趙州問僧：「發足甚處？」僧云：「雪峰。」州云：「雪峰有何言句示人？」僧云：「尋常道：『盡十方世界是沙門一隻眼，你等諸人向甚處屙？』」州云：「闍黎若迴，寄個鍬子去。」師云：「彼彼相助。」頌曰：「對面不相識，千里卻同風。若無河北輪刀手，誰解幫扶老雪峰？」紫湖門下立牌，牌上書云：「紫湖有狗，上取人頭，中取人腰，下取人腳，擬議則喪身失命。」有新到纔相看，湖便喝云：「看狗。」僧纔回首，湖便歸方丈。師云：「紫湖可謂老婆心切，爭奈無人捨命？」李居士請師於看狗處下語，師直前一摑。又云：「幸是老僧。」又云：「業畜不得無禮。」又於地上作󵐘相，隨以腳抹卻，又以手舉腰帶云：「個是五百文買底。」頌曰：「紫湖一隻狗，牙長善抖擻。誰論跖與堯，彌勒遭一口。」睦州因秀才相看，云：「會二十四家書。」州以拄杖空中點一點，云：「會麼？」秀才罔措。州云：「又道會二十四家書，永字八法也不識。」師云：「睦州者一點，莫道秀才家，便是佛來也不敢正眼覷著。」又云：「如蟲禦木。」頌曰：「一點分明露，其如識字多。若將八法論，鷂子過新羅。」葉縣省禪師問僧云：「日暮投林，朝離何處？」僧云：「某甲不曾學禪。」師云：「生身入地獄。」師云：「且道是者僧入地獄，是葉縣入地獄？」頌曰：「學禪不學禪，蜂蜜比糖甜。生身入地獄，千足與萬足。」楚圓禪師冬日榜示，僧堂前作此相，若人識得，不離四威儀中。師云：「當時若見，脫草鞋蘸水向上一擦。」頌曰：「天皇皇，地皇皇，我家有個夜啼郎。往來君子讀一遍，安眠穩睡到天光。」

Senses.Explanation: One can stand face to face without recognition and still share a current across great distance. Wuyi and Tianan bring the near-and-far contrast into their present sermons. Yikui asks who shares the wind, while Hanke uses the pair to open his own case verse.

Senses.Note: Three stronger works connect the phrase with disbelief, hesitation, and failure to know; one capping verse is retained for its distinct contrast with the slightest contrivance.

Occurrences.Kwic: 故此一心法門。如鏡頓現。不待次第。如印頓成。更無前後。一見一切見。一聞一切聞。不俟推尋。若待了達而成。皆為權漸。若能觀於心性之一。則是一道甚深。即正道之一。是唯一之一。千佛同轍。今古不易之一道也。亦云一路涅槃門。亦云一道出生死。又名大佛頂首楞嚴王具足萬行。十方如來一門超出。妙莊嚴路。猶如百華共成一蜜。故知萬法同會斯宗。若諦了之。一切在我。昇沈去住。任意隨緣。示聖現凡。出生入死。變化難測。運無作之神通。隱顯同時。闡如幻之三昧。是非冥合。逆順同歸。語默卷舒。常順一真之道。治生產業。不違實相之門。運用施為。念念而未離法界。行住坐臥。步步而常在其中。若不信之人。對面千里。如寒山子詩云。可貴天然物。獨一無伴侶。促之在方寸。延之一切處。汝若不信受。相逢不相遇。如明達之者。寓目關懷。悉能先覺。若未遇之子。可以事知。舉動施為。未甞間斷。如蔡順。字君仲。以孝聞。順少孤。養母。常出求薪。有客卒至。母望順不還。乃嚙其指。順即心動。棄薪馳歸。跪問其故。母曰。有急客來。吾嚙指以悟汝耳。又唐裴敬彝。父為陳王典所殺。敬彝時在城。忽自覺。流涕不食。謂人曰。我大人凡有痛處。吾即不安。今日心痛。手足皆廢。事在不測。遂歸覲。父果已死。又唐張志安。居鄉閭稱孝。差為里尹。在縣忽稱母疾急。縣令問。志安曰。母有疾志安亦病。志安適患心痛。是以知母有疾。令拘之

Occurrences.Kwic: 則不懺罪而罪滅河沙，越化城而便登寶所。秪如應物無私，甚處見他端的？即是錦衣公子貴，林下道人高。」復舉：「三祖僧粲大師問二祖云：『弟子身纏風恙，乞師懺罪。』祖云：『將罪來，與汝懺。』粲云：『覓罪性了不可得。』祖云：『與汝懺罪竟。』大眾！古人拔出眼中屑，抽卻腦後釘，雖證得罪福皆空，視身無我，撿點將來，未免猶在半途。今者座前陳公子入山飯僧，請法懺罪，誓明生死大事，冀其進道無魔，且喜身力強壯，氣宇如王，既無罪性可覓，山僧亦不好肉剜瘡，豈不出他古人頭地？為甚如此？端坐受供養，施主常安樂。」除夕，小參。拈拄杖，云：「結交頭，一句子，和盤托出來，不惜拖泥水。佇思停機，對面千里，快鷂俊鷹趁不及，迅雷豈待掩雙耳？」復卓一卓，云：「急薦取，知音何用頻為舉？」元旦，自覺監院募供法衣至，上堂。乃云：「元正啟祚，慶無不宜，衣好是新底，人好是舊底，老盧把住曹溪後，須信人人總有之。大功不宰，大化無為，拈來不費纖毫力，不是苦心人不知。」解制，上堂。「結卻布袋，何處叫屈？更待解開，還遭活埋。不結不解是活埋，不去不住是活埋。踏翻關捩子，透過祖師關，猶是堆上見堆，土上添土。要識山僧落處麼？從來不打禾山鼓。」一揆禪師語錄卷四終一揆禪師語錄卷五嗣法門人成定等編住潭州神鼎資聖禪寺四住潭州神鼎資聖禪寺昱林禪徒廣東募鑄千僧大鍋，到山啟建華嚴勝會，巴陵張仲公開

Senses.Explanation: A thousand miles apart face-to-face describes separation despite immediate proximity. Yongming Yanshou applies it to a person who does not trust what is directly present; Yikui Yuankui joins it to hesitation; Guyin Yuncong contrasts those who know with those who remain far away. The retained capping verse makes even a hair of contrivance produce the same distance.

Senses.Explanation: To submit a failed showing is to be publicly charged with, or made to concede, a particular failure in an encounter or address. Zhanran Yuancheng refuses another failed showing after the proclamation; Juelang Daosheng contrasts exposing ancestral failures with submitting one; Xutang Zhiyu charges Shakyamuni with submitting one at death; and Yuanwu Keqin applies the phrase to a clumsy public display. The lay official Feng Ji directs the accusation at Dahui Zonggao, while a genuinely unnamed monk directs it at Xutang Zhiyu. Each verdict remains limited to the showing under review.

Occurrences.Kwic: 土於億劫，贊皇圖於永年。誘引諸子，推排出火宅之門；拯拔迷流，踊躍登菩提之岸。且道畢竟從甚麼處建立？良久，云：拈出紅爐一點雪，長作人間六月冰。復舉：開元瑩禪師上堂語云：有一面鏡，到處懸掛。凡聖不來，誰上誰下？拈拄杖，云：這箇是拄杖，那箇是鏡？良久，云：萬古碧潭空界月，再三撈摝始應知。師云：歷劫無名，彰為古鏡。只要諸人知有，不為他影子所惑。瑩禪師大有為人處，山僧今日亦有一偈，不免舉似大眾：有一面鏡，到處懸掛。凡聖普現，非內非外。豎拂子，云：這箇是鏡，喚甚麼作拂子？還委悉麼？分明覿面別無真，休更迷頭猶認影。下座。多寶佛塔合尖陞座，師云：浮圖再造，多寶獨露全身；舍利斯藏，釋迦已分半座。壇場嚴淨，即是三變淨土；緇素雲集，何異十方分身？風鳴萬竅，如來親說法華；鳥噪千林，寶塔出聲讚善。古今一際，凡聖一源，體用一如，因果一法，靈山一會，儼然未散也。更看巍巍寶頂高踞七級之巔，燦燦金光遍照普天之下，直使有眼者見、有耳者聞、有心者知、有口者說，乃至童子嬉戲散心念佛，以及合郡官民紳士、男女老幼施食施財、搬磚運土，凡於此塔舉一念、捨一錢、用一力者，皆在如來授記之中，不特人天勝福而已。諸人還自信麼？良久，云：我不敢輕於汝等，汝等皆當作佛。下座。翠巖寺建殿陞梁示眾，師云：一毛端上，現寶王剎，百福莊嚴，普天歡洽。梁柱枋桷，主伴重重，共相成

Occurrences.Kwic: 於長沙之鹿苑。當時衲子倔強如仰山者，猶下之而呼以為岑大蟲云。為之贊曰：長沙大蟲，聲威甚重，獨眠空林，百獸震恐。寂子兒癡，見不知畏，引手捋鬚，幾缺其耳。大空小空，是虎是你，如備與覺，可撩其尾。嗟今衲子，眼如裴旻，但見其彪，安識虎真？我拜公像，非存非沒，百尺竿頭，行塵勃勃。白雲端禪師曰：天下叢林之興，大智禪師力也。祖堂當設達磨初祖之像於其中，大智禪師像西向，開山尊宿像東向，得其宜也。不當止設開山尊宿，而略其祖宗耳。雲居祐禪師曰：吾觀諸方長老示滅，必塔其骸。山川有限，而人死無窮，百千年之下，塔將無所容。於是於宏覺塔之東作卵塔，曰：凡住持者，自非生身不壞，火浴雨舍利者，皆以骨石填於此。其西又作卵塔，曰：凡眾僧化，皆藏骨石於此。謂之三塔。二大老識度高遠，可為後世法。然孤論難持，犯眾難成，卒必有賞音者，吾將觀焉。東京覺嚴寺有誠法師，講華嚴經，歷席最久，學者依以揚聲。其為人純至，少緣飾，高行遠識，近世講人，莫有居其右者。元祐初，高麗僧統航海至，上表乞傳持賢首宗教，歸本國流通。奉聖旨下兩街，舉可以授法者。有司以師為宜，上表辭免曰：臣雖刻意講學，識趣淺陋，特以年運已往，妄為學者所推。今異國名僧，航海問道，宜得高識博聞者為之師。竊見杭州慧因院僧道源，精練教乘，旁通外學，舉以自代，實允公議。奉聖旨依所乞，勑差朝奉郎揚傑館伴，至錢

Occurrences.Kwic: 州云：「田庫奴！甚麼處是揀擇？」僧無語。人頑似鐵，官法如爐，禾熟登場不納租。米裏有虫，麥裏有麩，田庫奴至道無難。會也麼？趙州。僧問：「如何是趙州？」州云：「東門、南門、西門、北門。」東西南北是門頭，問趙州兮答趙州。三四百條花柳巷，二三千處管絃樓。憲宗迎佛，舍利現五色光，百辟皆賀，唯韓愈端立。帝問：「百僚皆賀，卿為甚不賀？」師代云：「臣已賀了。」愈云：「臣曾看佛書來，佛光非青黃赤白等相，此是龍神荷助之光。」帝云：「如何是佛光？」愈無對。師代云：「陛下問處便是。」此光不是佛光，群臣莫我敬王。陛下問處便是，管取龍顏大喜。

Senses.Explanation: Relics are material remains associated with cremation, memorial storage, or public veneration. Weilin Daopei says relics are stored in a newly completed pagoda. In a quotation preserved by Huihong, Yunju Yuanyou distinguishes cremations that yield relics from ordinary bone-and-stone burial. Faxi Yin raises the imperial reception of the Buddha’s relics in verse, and a lamp biography reports relics after Miaofeng Zhishan’s cremation.
